aIDBSAVSPCR.description: Average selling price, all industries, current
aIDBSAVSPCR.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: Average Selling Price, All Industries, Current Period — net balance of firms reporting selling-price increases vs decreases.
aIDBSAVSPCR.how_to_use: Leading indicator of producer-price inflation and CPI goods-component (1-3 month lead). Sustained net positive readings flag pricing-power return; net negative signals competitive deflation. BI watches as inflation-momentum gauge.

aIDBSAVSPFU.description: Average selling price, all industries, future
aIDBSAVSPFU.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: Average Selling Price, All Industries, Future Period — forward-looking pricing intention from firms.
aIDBSAVSPFU.how_to_use: Leads CPI by ~3 months. Most market-relevant inflation-expectation series at the firm level. Used alongside household inflation expectations (aIDCSGENPR6, aIDPREXFR6M) for triangulated forward inflation reads.

aIDCAPUIND.description: Business Surveys, capacity utilization, all industries
aIDCAPUIND.meaning: Indonesia business survey series: Business Surveys, capacity utilization, all industries. Captures business-sector activity, expectations, or conditions.
aIDCAPUIND.how_to_use: Indonesia business surveys (BI's SKDU, S&P Global PMI, BPS sectoral surveys) provide forward-looking and current-state diffusion indicators. Net positive readings = expansion. Pair with hard-data complements for triangulated reads.

aIDBSBAAGRF.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Agriculture, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead expectation for agriculture sector. ~13% of GDP, ~28% of employment (low-productivity formal-informal mix).
aIDBSBAAGRF.how_to_use: Weather (El Niño/La Niña), commodity prices (CPO crude palm oil, rubber), and harvest cycles are dominant drivers. Volatile quarterly. Pair with palm-oil futures and rice-price tracking.

aIDBSBACTCR.meaning: Bank Indonesia Real Sector Business Activity Survey: All Industries, Current Period — the headline SBT (Saldo Bersih Tertimbang, weighted net balance). Quarterly survey of ~2,500 firms across 9 sectors. Released ~6 weeks after quarter-end.
aIDBSBACTCR.how_to_use: THE headline BI quarterly business-conditions print. Net balance: % reporting expansion minus % reporting contraction. Above zero = net positive activity. Indonesia SBT typically runs 5-15 in expansion years. Used by BI itself in MPC deliberations and quoted in Monetary Policy Reports. Cross-check against monthly S&P Global PMI for triangulated business-cycle reads.

aIDBSBACTFU.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: All Industries, Future Period — forward-looking version of the headline SBT. 1-quarter-ahead expectations from surveyed firms across all sectors.
aIDBSBACTFU.how_to_use: Leads aIDBSBACTCR (current SBT) by 1 quarter and aIDCGDPYD/A by 2 quarters. Sharp drops below 5 are recession-warning signals — Indonesia hasn't seen this outside crises (1998, 2020). Pair with current SBT — divergence (current high, future falling) signals cycle peak approaching.

aIDBSBACONF.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Construction, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead construction-sector activity expectation. ~11% of GDP, highly cyclical.
aIDBSBACONF.how_to_use: Leads construction GVA growth (aIDVADCONS/C) by 1 quarter. Sensitive to BI rate cycle and infrastructure-spending pipeline. Used in tracking property-cycle and government-spending implementation.

aIDBSBAESGW.description: Business activities, electricity, gas & water, future
aIDBSBAESGW.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Electricity, Gas & Water, Future Period — utilities sector forward expectation. Small share (~1%) but stable.
aIDBSBAESGW.how_to_use: Low cyclicality. Tracks PLN (state electricity utility) and gas-distribution activity. Useful for cross-validating broader business-conditions trends.

aIDBSBAFILB.description: Business activities, finance, leasing and business services, future
aIDBSBAFILB.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Finance, Leasing and Business Services, Future Period — financial-sector forward expectation. ~4% of GDP.
aIDBSBAFILB.how_to_use: Tracks financialization of the economy. Bank profitability cycles, capital-markets activity (IDX trading volume), and insurance sector growth drive this. Watch alongside JCI for financial-sector cycle.

aIDBSBAMNID.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Manufacturing Industry, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead manufacturing-sector activity expectation. Indonesia's largest sector at ~20% of GDP.
aIDBSBAMNID.how_to_use: Leads manufacturing GVA growth (aIDVADGM/C) by 1 quarter. Pair with S&P Global Manufacturing PMI (aIDPMIT/A) — when both move in same direction, signal is robust; divergences are usually resolved within 1-2 months.

aIDBSBAMIQE.description: Business activities, mining and quarrying, future
aIDBSBAMIQE.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Mining and Quarrying, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead expectation for the highly cyclical mining sector. ~10% of GDP, highly correlated with global commodity prices.
aIDBSBAMIQE.how_to_use: Sensitive to global coal/nickel/oil/palm-oil prices. Leads mining GVA growth (aIDVADMIN/C). Combined with commodity-price moves, the most reliable Indonesia sector-cycle leading indicator.

aIDBSBASRVF.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Services Sector, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead services-sector activity expectation. Services are ~45% of Indonesia GDP.
aIDBSBASRVF.how_to_use: Largest single sector in expectations. Coincides with services GVA growth. Less cyclical than manufacturing/construction but still meaningful for total-GDP tracking.

aIDBSBATRHS.description: Business activities, trade, hotel and restaurant, future
aIDBSBATRHS.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Trade, Hotel and Restaurant, Future Period — distributive-trades and hospitality-sector forward expectation.
aIDBSBATRHS.how_to_use: Best leading indicator for retail sales (aIDRSLSAR) and tourism-related GVA. Lebaran-Eid timing significantly affects this series — adjust for that when comparing across years.

aIDBSBATRCO.description: Business activities, transportation and communication, future
aIDBSBATRCO.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Transportation and Communication, Future Period — transport + telecom sector forward expectation. ~10% of GDP.
aIDBSBATRCO.how_to_use: Tracks logistics demand (cargo, passenger transport) and telecom-sector growth. Indonesia's archipelagic geography makes transport critical; logistics-cost reduction is a long-running policy theme.

aIDBSUOLCU.description: The usage of labor, all industries, current
aIDBSUOLCU.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: The Usage of Labor, All Industries, Current Period — net balance of firms reporting labor-usage increases vs decreases.
aIDBSUOLCU.how_to_use: Leading labor-market indicator at firm level. Coincides with formal-sector employment (aIDCEMFO/A) but releases earlier (BPS Sakernas only biannual). Sustained sub-zero readings flag formal-employment contraction ahead of BPS confirmation.

aIDBSUOLFU.description: The usage of labor, all industries, future
aIDBSUOLFU.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: The Usage of Labor, All Industries, Future Period — forward-looking firm-level hiring intentions.
aIDBSUOLFU.how_to_use: Leads formal employment by 1-2 quarters. Among the most reliable Indonesia labor-market leading indicators given Sakernas's biannual frequency. Sub-zero with current SBT also sub-zero is a strong recession-leading signal.

aIDFPGTL.how_to_use: Country-risk reference. Indonesia ranks in the middle tier (around 70-80 out of ~180 countries). Used in sovereign-risk and operational-risk screening alongside other governance indicators.

aIDFPYPTP.meaning: Fragile States Index for Indonesia. Annual ranking by the Fund for Peace measuring state stability across cohesion, economic, political, and social dimensions.

aIDESGGS/C.description: ESG, Global Sustainable GDP- PPP per capita, $PPP/2017, in constant prices
aIDESGGS/C.meaning: ESG Global Sustainable GDP — PPP per capita, 2017 USD constant prices. LSEG measure adjusting GDP for sustainability factors (environmental degradation, resource depletion, social inequality).
aIDESGGS/C.how_to_use: Sustainability-adjusted welfare measure. Indonesia's 'sustainable GDP' lags reported GDP because of resource depletion (mining, deforestation). Used in green-GDP and natural-capital accounting analyses.

aIDESGGLR.meaning: ESG Global Score for Indonesia — LSEG aggregate ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) score. Combines emissions intensity, social-development indicators, and governance scores.
aIDESGGLR.how_to_use: Used by ESG-mandated investors for country-level screening. Indonesia's profile shaped by deforestation concerns (palm oil), coal-export reliance (transition risk), and improving governance trajectory. Track for ESG-flow direction in EM portfolios.

aIDEJGGSR.description: ESG, Global sustainable gap compared to reported GDP
aIDEJGGSR.meaning: ESG Global Sustainable Gap Compared to Reported GDP — gap between conventional GDP and sustainability-adjusted GDP, expressed as a percentage of conventional GDP.
aIDEJGGSR.how_to_use: Indonesia's sustainability gap reflects resource-extraction-driven growth. Wider gaps signal greater unsustainability. Watch alongside emissions trajectory (aIDESECOP) and deforestation metrics for total environmental-cost picture.

aIDZAWTOR.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.

aIDOBS085Q/A.meaning: Indonesia manufacturing-related series: Manufacturing, Industrial confidence indicator. Sectoral indicator covering manufacturing activity dimensions.
aIDOBS085Q/A.how_to_use: Use alongside the headline PMI (composite of S&P Global aIDPMI series) and BPS Industrial Production for triangulated manufacturing-cycle reads.

aIDPMIMAQ.description: Manufacturing Sector, S&P Global PMI, Manufacturing
aIDPMIMAQ.meaning: Indonesia manufacturing-related series: Manufacturing Sector, S&P Global PMI, Manufacturing. Sectoral indicator covering manufacturing activity dimensions.
aIDPMIMAQ.how_to_use: Use alongside the headline PMI (composite of S&P Global aIDPMI series) and BPS Industrial Production for triangulated manufacturing-cycle reads.

aIDPMIBOW.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Backlogs of work
aIDPMIBOW.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Backlogs of Work sub-index. Above 50 = backlogs rising; below 50 = backlogs falling.
aIDPMIBOW.how_to_use: Rising backlogs signal capacity-stretched producers (positive for output near-term but with risk of lost orders). Falling backlogs may signal weakening demand or improved efficiency. Pair with New Orders to distinguish.

aIDPMIBOW/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Backlogs of work, SA
aIDPMIBOW/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Backlogs of Work sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
aIDPMIBOW/A.how_to_use: Useful for distinguishing capacity-stretched vs demand-weakening regimes. Sustained sub-50 with falling New Orders confirms demand weakness; with stable New Orders suggests efficiency gains.

aIDPMIEMPM.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Employment sub-index. Tracks net hiring vs layoff intentions at surveyed manufacturers.
aIDPMIEMPM.how_to_use: Leads formal manufacturing employment (aIDEMPMF) by 1-2 months. Indonesian manufacturers often delay layoffs (rigid labor laws) so sub-50 sustained signals labor-market deterioration ahead of BPS Sakernas reporting.

aIDPMIEMPM/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Empl, SA
aIDPMIEMPM/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Employment sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA version of manufacturing-jobs sentiment.
aIDPMIEMPM/A.how_to_use: Smoothed monthly employment-momentum signal. Indonesia's structural under-50 readings 2014-2017 (post-commodity-bust deindustrialization) reverted in 2018+ as manufacturing recovered.

aIDPMIMFBR.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Future Output
aIDPMIMFBR.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Future Output sub-index. 12-month-forward output expectation from manufacturers.
aIDPMIMFBR.how_to_use: Most forward-looking PMI sub-component. Sustained drops signal sentiment deterioration ahead of orders/output sub-indices weakening. Indonesia's future-output index typically runs >60 (chronically optimistic) — sustained sub-55 readings are warning signals.

aIDPMIINPP.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Input prc
aIDPMIINPP.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Input Prices sub-index. Tracks changes in costs of materials, labor, energy paid by manufacturers.
aIDPMIINPP.how_to_use: Leading indicator for goods CPI and PPI inflation by 1-3 months. Sensitive to global commodity prices and IDR — sharp jumps signal upcoming pass-through to consumer prices. BI watches this for cost-push inflation signals.

aIDPMIINPP/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Input prc, SA
aIDPMIINPP/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Input Prices sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA cost-pressure gauge.
aIDPMIINPP/A.how_to_use: Indonesia's input-price index typically runs 55-60 (chronic mild input inflation). Spikes above 65 historically follow oil-price surges and IDR weakness — pre-cursor to faster CPI prints 1-2 quarters later.

aIDPMIEO.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, New exp orders
aIDPMIEO.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: New Export Orders sub-index. Tracks foreign demand for Indonesian manufactured goods.
aIDPMIEO.how_to_use: Sensitive to global PMI, China industrial activity, and CNY/IDR cross-rate. Diverges from total New Orders — when total holds but exports drop, domestic demand is the support; when exports hold but total drops, domestic weakness emerging.

aIDPMIEO/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, New exp orders, SA
aIDPMIEO/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia New Export Orders sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
aIDPMIEO/A.how_to_use: Tracks ASEAN-export cycle and China-demand cycle. Indonesia's export PMI sub-index has been more volatile than total New Orders post-2020 due to commodity-price-driven China demand swings.

aIDPMINORD.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, New orders
aIDPMINORD.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: New Orders sub-index. Captures month-on-month change in new business received by Indonesian manufacturers from domestic and foreign customers.
aIDPMINORD.how_to_use: Most-watched leading sub-index — leads headline PMI by 1-3 months at turning points and leads industrial-production growth (aIDCINDYG/CA) by 2-4 months. Sustained drops below 50 alongside falling output sub-index signal genuine demand weakness vs supply constraints.

aIDPMINORD/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, New orders, SA
aIDPMINORD/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia New Orders sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA version of the leading PMI sub-component. Smooths Lebaran/CNY distortions in the orders pulse.
aIDPMINORD/A.how_to_use: Best high-frequency forward-looking read on Indonesian manufacturing demand. Watch the spread vs Output sub-index — when New Orders < Output for sustained periods, it signals upcoming production cuts as backlogs run down.

aIDPMIOUT.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Output sub-index. Direct measure of changes in production volumes at Indonesian manufacturers.
aIDPMIOUT.how_to_use: Coincides with manufacturing GVA growth (aIDVADGM/C) — best cross-check of BPS Industrial Production Index (aIDCINDYG/CA) which has small-sample noise. Sustained sub-50 confirms manufacturing recession.

aIDPMIOUTPM.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Output prc
aIDPMIOUTPM.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Output Prices sub-index. Tracks pricing power — whether manufacturers are passing input costs through to selling prices.
aIDPMIOUTPM.how_to_use: Watch the spread vs Input Prices: when input prices rise faster than output prices, manufacturer margins are compressing (corporate-earnings risk). When output prices rise faster, demand is strong enough to support pass-through (inflation risk).

aIDPMIOUTPM/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Output prc, SA
aIDPMIOUTPM/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Output Prices sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA pricing-power gauge.
aIDPMIOUTPM/A.how_to_use: Cleanest signal of manufacturer pricing power. Sustained reading near 50 with elevated input prices = margin squeeze; >55 with elevated input = strong pass-through (often signals demand strength).

aIDPMIOUT/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Output, SA
aIDPMIOUT/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Output sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA version of the production-volume gauge.
aIDPMIOUT/A.how_to_use: Use for monthly tracking; Lebaran-month distortions are removed. Drop below 50 sustained for 3+ months has historically aligned with quarterly manufacturing GVA contraction.

aIDPMIQTYP.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Quantity of prchs
aIDPMIQTYP.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Quantity of Purchases sub-index. Tracks input-side purchasing activity (volume of materials bought).
aIDPMIQTYP.how_to_use: Active purchasing signals manufacturers gearing up for output. Sustained drops align with output cuts. Pair with Stocks of Purchases for full input-cycle picture.

aIDPMIQTYP/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Quantity of prchs, SA
aIDPMIQTYP/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Quantity of Purchases sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
aIDPMIQTYP/A.how_to_use: Smoothed manufacturer purchasing-activity gauge. Useful as raw-material-import predictor (aIDIMPRM).

aIDPMIFING.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Stocks of fnshd gds
aIDPMIFING.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Stocks of Finished Goods sub-index. Tracks inventory buildup at the producer end.
aIDPMIFING.how_to_use: Above 50 = inventory rising (potentially undesired demand weakness or planned stockpiling). Below 50 = inventory falling (strong demand draw). Pair with New Orders — when both fall, downside risk to output near-term.

aIDPMIFING/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Stocks of fnshd gds, SA
aIDPMIFING/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Stocks of Finished Goods sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
aIDPMIFING/A.how_to_use: Cleanest inventory signal. Watch for prolonged elevated readings as production-cut warning; persistent low readings as supply-tightness signal.

aIDPMIPUR.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Stocks of prchs
aIDPMIPUR.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Stocks of Purchases sub-index. Tracks raw-material inventory at producers (input-side stockpile).
aIDPMIPUR.how_to_use: Rising stocks of purchases signal manufacturers anticipating production ramp; falling signal de-stocking ahead of expected demand weakness. Used in PMI composite alongside delivery times.

aIDPMIPUR/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Stocks of prchs, SA
aIDPMIPUR/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Stocks of Purchases sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
aIDPMIPUR/A.how_to_use: Use for trend in raw-material inventory accumulation. Surges typically precede production peaks by 1-2 months.

aIDPMISDT.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Suppliers' dlvy times
aIDPMISDT.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Suppliers' Delivery Times sub-index. Inverted scale: above 50 = lengthening delivery times (supply-chain stress); below 50 = improving delivery times.
aIDPMISDT.how_to_use: Lengthening delivery times correlate with strong demand or supply-chain disruptions. Indonesia's index spiked 2021-22 (global supply-chain shock); normalized post-2023. Watch alongside Input Prices for supply-side stress signals.

aIDPMISDT/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Suppliers' dlvy times, SA
aIDPMISDT/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Suppliers' Delivery Times sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
aIDPMISDT/A.how_to_use: SA version smooths Lebaran-related shipping disruptions. Useful for spotting genuine supply-chain stress vs holiday-driven delivery delays.

aIDPMIT.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI Headline — composite diffusion index of New Orders, Output, Employment, Suppliers' Delivery Times, and Stocks of Purchases. Survey of ~400 Indonesian manufacturing companies, released first business day of each month at 09:00 WIB.
aIDPMIT.how_to_use: THE most-watched Indonesia high-frequency activity gauge. Above 50 = manufacturing expanding, below 50 = contracting. Indonesia PMI typically runs 50-54 in expansion (post-2017 average). Sustained sub-50 prints (3+ months) historically signal manufacturing-recession. Surprise vs Reuters consensus drives IDR and JCI same-day.

aIDPMIT/A.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Total, SA
aIDPMIT/A.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI Headline, seasonally adjusted — the official released headline number markets watch. SA version smooths month-of-Lebaran and Chinese New Year distortions.
aIDPMIT/A.how_to_use: The headline release. Same data as aIDPMIT but SA-adjusted — what economists and market commentary cite. Sub-50 readings have correctly preceded Indonesia's small post-2017 manufacturing contractions. Pair with BI's Real Sector Business Activity Survey (aIDBSBACTCR) for the broader business-sentiment picture.

aIDCSBUICON.meaning: Business Conditions, 6 Months Hence — sub-index of BI Consumer Survey capturing forward-looking business-conditions assessment.
aIDCSBUICON.how_to_use: Forward-looking sub-component. Track alongside CEI (aIDCONCE) for broader expectations read.

aIDCSBYDUBG.meaning: Buying Durable Goods Conditions, Present — sub-index measuring whether households view current conditions as appropriate for big-ticket purchases.
aIDCSBYDUBG.how_to_use: Leading indicator of durable-goods spending (autos, appliances, furniture). Falls during high-inflation or rate-hike periods.

aIDCONIAR.description: Consumer Confidence Index - Actual, Index, IDR
aIDCONIAR.meaning: Consumer Confidence Index — Reuters poll-anchored 'actual' release. Same conceptual measure as aIDCONCF.
aIDCONIAR.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Reuters polls economists ahead of the BI release; the 'actual' is set when BI publishes.

aIDCONCF.meaning: Consumer Confidence Index (CCI) — Bank Indonesia monthly Survey of Consumer Confidence (SK). Composite of Current Conditions Index (CCI-Present) and Consumer Expectations Index (CEI). Released first week of each month.
aIDCONCF.how_to_use: Most-watched Indonesia consumer-sentiment gauge. Above 100 = optimistic, below 100 = pessimistic. Indonesia consumer confidence has been resilient: typically 110-130. Sharp drops below 100 (1998, 2008, 2020) signal economic crisis. Sub-indices: business conditions, employment, income — track separately.

aIDCONCE.meaning: Consumer Expectations Index (CEI / IEK) — forward-looking sub-component of BI's consumer confidence survey. Captures households' 6-month outlook on income, employment, and business conditions.
aIDCONCE.how_to_use: Leads household consumption growth by 1-2 quarters. Sub-100 readings sustained for 3+ months signal upcoming consumption slowdown. Pair with Present Conditions index (aIDCONCFPT) — when expectations diverge below current conditions, consumer cycle is rolling over.

aIDCONCFPT.meaning: Present Conditions Index (IKE) — sub-component of BI's consumer confidence survey assessing current economic conditions, employment, and major-purchase appropriateness.
aIDCONCFPT.how_to_use: Coincides with current consumption activity (vs CEI which leads). Pairs with retail sales, vehicle sales for current-state cross-check. Higher than expectations = late-cycle pattern; lower = early-cycle.

aIDCSCRICMP.meaning: Current Incomes, Present — sub-index measuring household current-income perceptions.
aIDCSCRICMP.how_to_use: Pair with income expectations (aIDCSINC6MN). Divergence (current high, expectations low) signals income-cycle peak.

aIDCSEMCNPR.meaning: Employment Conditions, Present — sub-index assessing current labor-market perceptions.
aIDCSEMCNPR.how_to_use: Track for current labor-market health from household side. Coincides with unemployment trends.

aIDCSEMP6MN.meaning: Employment, 6 Months Hence — household forward-looking employment-prospects sub-index.
aIDCSEMP6MN.how_to_use: Leading labor-market indicator. Drops below current-conditions sub-index signal upcoming labor-market deterioration.

aIDCSINC6MN.meaning: Income Expectations, 6 Months Hence — sub-index of BI Consumer Survey capturing forward-looking household income optimism.
aIDCSINC6MN.how_to_use: Leading indicator for consumer spending. When income expectations fall while current incomes hold steady, households start saving more — consumption decelerates 1-2 quarters later. Diverges sharply from current-incomes (aIDCSCRICMP) at cycle turning points.

aIDPREXFR6M.description: Price expectations for next 6 mos., overall prices
aIDPREXFR6M.meaning: Price Expectations for Next 6 Months, Overall — household 6-month-ahead price expectation index from BI's Consumer Survey.
aIDPREXFR6M.how_to_use: Slightly longer horizon than aIDCSGENPR6. Both should track each other; divergence signals near vs medium-term inflation worry. Useful as a cross-check for BI's quarterly inflation forecasts published in the Monetary Policy Report.

aIDCSGENPR6.meaning: Price Expectations, General, 3 months hence — household inflation expectation sub-index from BI's Consumer Survey. Captures anticipated overall price changes.
aIDCSGENPR6.how_to_use: Indonesia's inflation expectations are sticky around BI's target band (1.5-3.5% since 2024). Sharp jumps signal expectation un-anchoring — concerning for BI policy. Pair with aIDPREXFR6M (6-month version) for short vs medium horizon read.

aIDCCIPSOR.description: LSEG / Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index (CSI)
aIDCCIPSOR.meaning: LSEG/Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index (CSI) for Indonesia — alternative consumer-sentiment gauge from Ipsos surveys.
aIDCCIPSOR.how_to_use: Cross-check against BI's Consumer Confidence Index (aIDCONCF). Smaller-sample but good for triangulation.

aIDIPSORA.description: LSEG / Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index (PCSI)
aIDIPSORA.meaning: LSEG/Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index (PCSI) — companion to aIDCCIPSOR.
aIDIPSORA.how_to_use: Cross-check. Use either for tertiary consumer-sentiment read.

aIDCLEAD.meaning: Composite Leading Indicators (Trend Restored) — OECD-compiled forward-looking activity index. Combines yield curve, industrial inputs, surveys, asset prices.
aIDCLEAD.how_to_use: OECD CLI for Indonesia leads activity by 6-9 months. Sustained sub-100 readings precede slowdowns. Use alongside Manufacturing PMI for triangulated cycle read.

aIDFRDST.meaning: Global Freedom Status — Freedom House annual freedom-of-expression and political-rights ranking for Indonesia. Reference series for governance research.
aIDFRDST.how_to_use: Indonesia rated 'Partly Free' in recent Freedom House assessments. Track for governance/political-risk profiling. Not a macro indicator.

aIDCARYAR.description: Domestic Vehicle Sales - Cars- Actual, Chg Y/Y
aIDCARYAR.meaning: Domestic Vehicle Sales, Cars — YoY change. Reuters poll-anchored 'actual' release tracking GAIKINDO car sales data.
aIDCARYAR.how_to_use: Indonesia car market ~800k units/year. Toyota, Daihatsu, Honda dominate. Watch for YoY swings >20% as cycle inflection signal.

aIDDVEHMOT.meaning: Domestic Sales of Motorcycles — Indonesia is the world's third-largest motorcycle market behind India and China. ~5-6M units/year sold.
aIDDVEHMOT.how_to_use: Honda + Yamaha dominate (~95% combined market share). Tracks middle-class Indonesian household formation closely. Surges during commodity-export booms (rural-area income gains).

aIDDVEHCAR.meaning: Motor Vehicles, Domestic Sales of Cars — passenger car sales level (excludes commercial vehicles, motorcycles).
aIDDVEHCAR.how_to_use: Pre-2014 peak ~1.2M units; current ~800k. 'Middle-income trap' in autos — sustained mid-2010s stagnation reflects post-commodity-supercycle structural slowdown. Watch EV transition (Wuling, Hyundai launching local production).

aIDMBKYAP.meaning: Motor Vehicles, Motorcycles — YoY change in motorcycle sales.
aIDMBKYAP.how_to_use: Motorcycle YoY is one of the best high-frequency consumer-spending gauges for Indonesia. Tracks rural and small-business income closely. Honda/Yamaha report monthly to AISI (Indonesian Motorcycle Industry Association).

aIDCBRRA.meaning: 7-Day Reverse Repo Rate (release vintage in BoP file) — same as aIDRREP7. Released alongside BoP statistics in some BI publications.
aIDCBRRA.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary policy-rate series (aIDBIR, aIDRREP7).

aIDCAFBALA.meaning: BoP Capital and Financial Balance — combined capital account + financial account. Mirror of current account balance under accounting identity.
aIDCAFBALA.how_to_use: Should be roughly equal magnitude (opposite sign) to current account. Decompose into capital + financial for source-of-funding analysis.

aIDCURAGEXP.meaning: BoP: Exports of Goods (FOB) — current-account goods exports on FOB basis. Same conceptual measure as aIDCEXBA.
aIDCURAGEXP.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCEXBA. FOB basis (Free on Board, ex-shipping) aligns with international trade-statistics standard.

aIDCAA.description: Balance of Payments, Current Account, % of GDP
aIDCAA.meaning: Current Account Balance as a percentage of GDP — the headline external-balance gauge. Released quarterly by Bank Indonesia. Combines goods balance, services balance, primary income, and secondary income.
aIDCAA.how_to_use: Indonesia's current account ranges from -3% to +1% of GDP across the commodity cycle. Sustained deficits beyond -3% have historically preceded IDR stress (1998 crisis, 2013 taper tantrum). Currently near balance. Watch the goods balance (largest component) for the cyclical driver — commodity export prices dominate.

aIDBOPAA.meaning: Balance of Payments: Overall Balance — sum of current account + capital account + financial account + errors and omissions. Reflects net FX reserve change in a given quarter.
aIDBOPAA.how_to_use: When overall balance is positive, BI accumulates reserves; negative, BI draws down reserves to defend IDR. Should match the change in FX reserves over the same period (with some discrepancies for valuation effects). Persistent negative overall balance flags external-financing stress.

aIDBPBALAA.meaning: Balance, Overall Balance — alternative release of overall BoP balance. Same conceptual measure as aIDBOPAA.
aIDBPBALAA.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data. Should equal change in FX reserves (with valuation adjustments).

aIDCURAC.meaning: Current Account Balance — alternative release of CA balance level (companion to aIDCURAAB and aIDCCURB/A).
aIDCURAC.how_to_use: Cross-check against the standardized series. Use whichever has fresher data.

aIDBPCGDPR.description: Current Account, Balance, Current account balance to GDP, % of GDP
aIDBPCGDPR.meaning: Current Account Balance to GDP — same conceptual measure as aIDCAA in alternative release. The headline external-balance gauge.
aIDBPCGDPR.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCAA. Use either for tracking external-vulnerability cycle.

aIDEXPBGA.meaning: Current Account: Goods, Exports (FOB) — same as aIDCURAGEXP at different release vintage.
aIDEXPBGA.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences are typically minor.

aIDCURAGIMP.meaning: Current Account: Goods, Imports (FOB) — current-account goods imports on FOB basis. Same as aIDCIMBA.
aIDCURAGIMP.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCIMBA. FOB framing aligns with international trade-statistics conventions; CIF (cost-insurance-freight) differences are minor.

aIDCUGTBAL.meaning: Current Account: Goods Trade Balance — net goods balance (exports minus imports) on CA basis. Same as aIDCBOPA.
aIDCUGTBAL.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCBOPA. The CA-basis goods balance is the source of Indonesia's external surplus; persistent commodity-export driver.

aIDBPSRVNA.meaning: Current Account: Services Net — services balance. Indonesia runs a persistent services deficit (~$15-20B/year) driven by transport (freight + tourism outflows) and business services.
aIDBPSRVNA.how_to_use: Tourism is the largest single services sub-account (Bali, etc.) — recovered post-COVID but pre-pandemic peak still elusive. Travel deficit (Indonesians traveling abroad spending more than foreign visitors) widens with IDR strength. Services trade development is a long-term competitiveness goal.

aIDBPEROMA.meaning: Errors and Omissions — residual in the BoP that balances current account + capital + financial accounts. Captures unrecorded transactions, valuation effects, timing differences.
aIDBPEROMA.how_to_use: Persistent large negative E&O suggests unrecorded capital outflows (potentially capital flight). Indonesia's E&O ranges $-3B to $+3B per quarter; sustained large negative readings prompt BI investigation.

aIDBPFIACA.meaning: Financial Account Balance — net total of FDI + portfolio + other investment flows. The funding side of the BoP that finances current account deficits.
aIDBPFIACA.how_to_use: Should be roughly equal in magnitude (opposite sign) to current account by accounting identity. When financial account inflows fall short of current account deficit, FX reserves draw down to fill the gap — direct pressure on IDR. Decompose to identify whether stress is FDI (structural) or portfolio (cyclical).

aIDBPDRIVA.description: Financial Account, Direct Investment, Balance, Net
aIDBPDRIVA.meaning: Financial Account: Direct Investment, Net — net FDI inflows minus outflows. Indonesia is structurally a net FDI recipient.
aIDBPDRIVA.how_to_use: Net FDI inflows ~$15-25B/year. Key sources: Singapore (largest, often pass-through), China, Japan, US. Sectors: minerals (smelters), manufacturing, finance. FDI is the most stable component of the financial account — sudden FDI slowdowns signal investor-confidence loss (e.g., resource nationalism shifts, regulatory unpredictability).

aIDBPOTIVA.description: Financial Account, Other Investment, Balance, Net
aIDBPOTIVA.meaning: Financial Account: Other Investment, Net — non-FDI, non-portfolio cross-border flows. Includes loans, trade credits, currency/deposits.
aIDBPOTIVA.how_to_use: Captures interbank lending, syndicated loans, and commercial credit flows. Volatile; smooths out in annual aggregates. Watch alongside FDI and portfolio flows for total financial-account composition.

aIDBPPRIVA.description: Financial Account, Portfolio Investment, Balance, Net
aIDBPPRIVA.meaning: Financial Account: Portfolio Investment, Net — net flows in equities and debt securities. The 'hot money' component most sensitive to global risk sentiment and rate differentials.
aIDBPPRIVA.how_to_use: Highly volatile quarterly. Foreign investors hold ~14% of SBN (gov bonds) and ~25-30% of JCI free-float — large outflows during EM stress (2013 taper tantrum, 2018 Powell tightening, 2022 USD strength). Sustained portfolio outflows alongside IDR weakness signal rising EM stress.

aIDCCURB/A.meaning: Current Account Balance, level — quarterly absolute current account balance in USD. Sums goods + services + primary income + secondary income (transfers).
aIDCCURB/A.how_to_use: Track in USD terms for cross-country comparison. Indonesia runs current account deficits in commodity downcycles (-$30B/year in 2013-14) and small surpluses in upcycles (+$10B in 2022). The goods surplus (~$30-50B/year on commodities) is offset by services deficits (tourism, transport) and primary income deficits (FDI dividend repatriation).

aIDCCURPB/A.description: Current Account Balance, quarter on quarter, Standardized, Absolute change
aIDCCURPB/A.meaning: Current Account Balance, QoQ absolute change — change in CA balance vs prior quarter.
aIDCCURPB/A.how_to_use: Track for sequential momentum. Sharp QoQ deteriorations signal commodity-cycle peaks or sudden import surges.

aIDCCURYB/A.description: Current Account Balance, year on year, Standardized, Absolute change
aIDCCURYB/A.meaning: Current Account Balance, year-over-year absolute change — change in CA level vs same quarter year ago.
aIDCCURYB/A.how_to_use: Cleaner annual trend signal. Sustained YoY deterioration (>$5B) flags external-vulnerability buildup.

aIDOBPCKL/A.description: BOP Current account as a % of GDP, SA
aIDOBPCKL/A.meaning: BoP Current Account as % of GDP, seasonally adjusted — same as aIDCAA in SA framing.
aIDOBPCKL/A.how_to_use: SA version smooths quarterly seasonality. Use for trend analysis. Cross-check against aIDCAA.

aIDFDIRTOA.meaning: Foreign Direct Investment — net FDI inflows. Same as aIDBPDRIVA in different framing.
aIDFDIRTOA.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDBPDRIVA. Indonesia is a structural net FDI recipient.

aIDCCURQ/A.description: Current Account Balance as a percentage of GDP, Standardized
aIDCCURQ/A.meaning: Current Account Balance as % of GDP (standardized) — companion to aIDCAA in alternative framing.
aIDCCURQ/A.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCAA. Use either for external-vulnerability tracking.

aIDCCURPQ/A.description: Current Account Balance as a percentage of GDP, quarter on quarter, Standardized
aIDCCURPQ/A.meaning: Current Account Balance as % of GDP, QoQ change — sequential deterioration/improvement of CA/GDP ratio.
aIDCCURPQ/A.how_to_use: Useful for tracking CA-cycle inflections at quarterly frequency. Indonesia CA/GDP swings 1-2pp through commodity cycles.

aIDCCURYQ/A.description: Current Account Balance as a percentage of GDP, year on year, Standardized
aIDCCURYQ/A.meaning: Current Account Balance as % of GDP, YoY change — change in CA/GDP ratio vs same quarter year ago.
aIDCCURYQ/A.how_to_use: Smoothed external-balance trend. Compare to BI's quarterly CA forecasts.

aIDCEXBPA.description: Exports of Goods, Balance of Payments Basis, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCEXBPA.meaning: Goods Exports (BoP basis), MoM percent change — month-over-month export-momentum signal.
aIDCEXBPA.how_to_use: Volatile (commodity prices, shipping timing). Smooth with 3-month average for trend.

aIDCEXBYA.description: Exports of Goods, Balance of Payments Basis, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCEXBYA.meaning: Goods Exports (BoP basis), YoY percent change — annual export-growth pace.
aIDCEXBYA.how_to_use: Cleaner trend than MoM. Indonesia's commodity-export cycles drive 30-50pp YoY swings (e.g., 2021-22 boom).

aIDCEXBA.description: Exports of Goods, Balance of Payments Basis, Standardized
aIDCEXBA.meaning: Goods Exports on BoP basis — total merchandise exports. Dominated by coal, palm oil, nickel, oil/gas, processed nickel products (post-2020 export-ban-driven downstream), manufactures, rubber.
aIDCEXBA.how_to_use: Most-watched single export driver: coal prices (Newcastle benchmark) — Indonesia is the world's largest thermal coal exporter. Palm oil follows malaysian/indonesian futures. Nickel surged post-2020 with EV battery demand and downstream value-add policies. China demand share (~25% of exports) — track Chinese steel and EV production for leading signal.

aIDCBOPA.description: Visible Trade Balance, Balance of Payments Basis, Standardized
aIDCBOPA.meaning: Visible (goods) Trade Balance on Balance of Payments basis — exports of goods minus imports of goods. Indonesia's primary external surplus driver, dominated by commodity exports.
aIDCBOPA.how_to_use: Released monthly by BPS (~3-week lag) — most-watched Indonesia external print. Persistent surplus on commodity exports (coal, palm oil, nickel). Falls when commodity prices weaken or when capital goods imports surge (infrastructure cycle). Track 3-month moving average for cleaner signal.

aIDCBOPPA.description: Visible Trade Balance, Balance of Payments Basis, month on month, Standardized, Absolute change
aIDCBOPPA.meaning: Visible Trade Balance (BoP basis), MoM absolute change — month-over-month change in goods trade balance.
aIDCBOPPA.how_to_use: Useful for tracking trade-balance momentum. Sharp MoM swings (>$2B) usually reflect commodity-price shifts or one-off shipment timing. Smooth with 3-month average.

aIDCBOPYA.description: Visible Trade Balance, Balance of Payments Basis, year on year, Standardized, Absolute change
aIDCBOPYA.meaning: Visible Trade Balance (BoP basis), YoY absolute change — change in goods trade balance vs same month a year ago.
aIDCBOPYA.how_to_use: Cleaner trend signal than MoM. Use to identify trade-cycle inflection points. Sustained YoY deterioration alongside IDR weakness flags external stress.

aIDCIMBPA.description: Imports of Goods, Balance of Payments Basis, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCIMBPA.meaning: Goods Imports (BoP basis), MoM percent change — high-frequency import-demand pulse.
aIDCIMBPA.how_to_use: Volatile. Smooth with 3-month average. Spikes around Lebaran-Eid period.

aIDCIMBYA.description: Imports of Goods, Balance of Payments Basis, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCIMBYA.meaning: Goods Imports (BoP basis), YoY percent change — annual import-growth pace.
aIDCIMBYA.how_to_use: Pro-cyclical with domestic demand and capital investment. Falls during IDR-weakness episodes.

aIDCIMBA.description: Imports of Goods, Balance of Payments Basis, Standardized
aIDCIMBA.meaning: Goods Imports on BoP basis — total merchandise imports. Largest categories: capital goods (machinery, transport equipment), raw materials (chemicals, base metals), oil/gas products (Indonesia is a net oil importer), consumer goods.
aIDCIMBA.how_to_use: Cyclical with domestic investment (capital goods imports lead GFCF) and oil prices (oil products import bill). Track non-oil-and-gas imports for cleaner signal of underlying demand. Sustained import surges relative to exports flag widening trade deficit.

aIDCBLODPR.description: Commercial Banks, Performance, loan to deposits ratio (%)
aIDCBLODPR.meaning: Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) for commercial banks — share of deposits being lent out. Indonesia regulatory norm is 78-92% (BI's macroprudential corridor).
aIDCBLODPR.how_to_use: Above 92% requires extra reserve provisioning under BI's RIM (Reserve Requirement based on Intermediation) rules. Below 78% means banks are sitting on excess liquidity. Recent system LDR ~85-90%. Higher LDR = banks lending more aggressively; rising LDR with deposit outflows flags liquidity stress.

aIDCRBCOF.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, claims on other sector, claims on other financial institutions
aIDCRBCOF.meaning: Commercial and Rural Banks: Claims on Other Sector, Other Financial Corporations — bank loans to non-bank financial institutions (insurance, asset managers, finance companies).
aIDCRBCOF.how_to_use: Tracks interconnections in financial system. Surge in claims on NBFIs may signal regulatory arbitrage or shadow-banking growth — OJK monitors.

aIDCRBLPS.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, claims on other sector, claims on private sectors, loans
aIDCRBLPS.meaning: Bank Claims on Local Government and State Enterprises — bank credit to public-sector entities (regional governments, SOEs like PLN, Pertamina, BUMN).
aIDCRBLPS.how_to_use: State enterprises like PLN, Pertamina are major bank borrowers. Concentration risk: top SOEs hold significant share of bank loan books.

aIDCRBCPNF.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, claims on other sector, claims on public non financial
aIDCRBCPNF.meaning: Bank Claims on Non-Financial Corporations — corporate-sector lending. The 'real economy' bank credit channel.
aIDCRBCPNF.how_to_use: Cyclical with capex investment cycles. Watch for sector concentration (mining, real estate, manufacturing). High concentration in property/CRE is a vulnerability.

aIDCRBCSL.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, claims on other sector, claims on state and local government
aIDCRBCSL.meaning: Bank Claims on Households — consumer + mortgage lending. Same concept as aIDCRDCONAA at different aggregation.
aIDCRBCSL.how_to_use: Track for household-leverage cycle. Indonesia household-credit-to-GDP ~17% — low but rising as financial inclusion deepens.

aIDCRBNCG.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, net claims on central government
aIDCRBNCG.meaning: Bank Net Claims on Central Government — banks' net position vs central government (gov bonds held minus government deposits).
aIDCRBNCG.how_to_use: Indonesia banks are large SBN (gov bond) holders post-2020. Surge in net claims on government during easing cycles signals 'crowding-in' of bank balance sheets into Treasury bonds vs lending.

aIDCRDAPPCC.meaning: Consumer credit approvals — share of total credit approvals going to households (mortgages, vehicle loans, personal loans, credit cards).
aIDCRDAPPCC.how_to_use: Track for household leverage cycle. Pre-2020 typically ~30-35% of total approvals. Surges during easing cycles when banks compete on consumer-loan rates. OJK monitors mortgage and auto-loan LTV (loan-to-value) caps for macroprudential signal — tight LTV slows this stat.

aIDCREDAPP.meaning: Total credit approvals — flow measure of new loan commitments by commercial banks. Leading indicator of stock-level outstanding credit.
aIDCREDAPP.how_to_use: Approval flow leads outstanding-credit stock by 1-3 months (drawdowns lag commitments). Sharp slowdowns in approvals signal bank risk aversion or weak loan demand — early warning for deceleration in lending. Pair with consumer-credit-approval (aIDCRDAPPCC) for retail vs business breakdown.

aIDCBCRDTA.description: Credit of commercial banks to non bank third party, total
aIDCBCRDTA.meaning: Total Credit of Commercial Banks to Non-Bank Third Parties — the headline bank credit aggregate. Includes corporate, SME, and household lending across all currency denominations. Published monthly by Bank Indonesia.
aIDCBCRDTA.how_to_use: Indonesia bank credit growth typically runs 8-12% YoY in normal cycles. Sub-5% signals weak loan demand or tight credit supply (often during BI hike cycles); >15% suggests aggressive easing. Pair with M2 — when credit grows faster than M2, banks are funding loans by drawing down liquidity buffers.

aIDLONYAR.description: Credit of commercial banks to non bank third party, total, Chg Y/Y
aIDLONYAR.meaning: Total Bank Credit, year-over-year change — pace of credit creation by commercial banks to non-bank third parties. The most-watched bank-lending growth indicator.
aIDLONYAR.how_to_use: Tracks the credit cycle. >12% YoY = expansionary; <5% = stalling. Compare to nominal GDP growth — credit-to-GDP gap widening signals overheating; narrowing signals deleveraging. BI watches this for systemic-stability signals; OJK (banking regulator) targets specific sectoral exposures.

aIDCBIDAR.meaning: Bank Indonesia Deposit Facility Rate — same conceptual measure as aIDRINTO in banking-data framing.
aIDCBIDAR.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDRINTO. The DF rate sets the floor of BI's interest rate corridor.

aIDCBILAR.meaning: Bank Indonesia Lending Facility Rate — same conceptual measure as aIDRREPO in banking-data framing.
aIDCBILAR.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDRREPO. The LF rate sets the ceiling of BI's interest rate corridor.

aIDMACBLCA.description: Monetary Authority Balance, claims on banks, liquidity credit
aIDMACBLCA.meaning: Monetary Authority Balance: Claims on Banks, Liquidity Credit — BI's lending to banks via repo and emergency facilities.
aIDMACBLCA.how_to_use: Spikes during liquidity stress (2020 COVID). BI's term repo and FX swap operations show up here. Persistent large balance signals systemic dollar/IDR funding pressure.

aIDOCRD.description: Outstanding credits of commercial banks, total
aIDOCRD.meaning: Outstanding credits of commercial banks, total — stock measure of bank loan book. Different framing from aIDCBCRDTA but tracks the same underlying credit aggregate.
aIDOCRD.how_to_use: Use either this or aIDCBCRDTA as the level measure; growth rates (aIDLONYAR) are the meaningful signal. Decompose by sector (working capital, investment, consumption) for cyclical decomposition — investment loans are the most rate-sensitive component.

aIDZQDIBA.description: IFDI, Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Assets
aIDZQDIBA.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator (IFDI): Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Assets. Reference data on Indonesia's Islamic finance ecosystem (Sharia-compliant banking, takaful insurance, sukuk markets, Islamic funds).
aIDZQDIBA.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.

aIDZQDIBP.description: IFDI, Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Full Fledged Banks
aIDZQDIBP.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator (IFDI): Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Full Fledged Banks. Reference data on Indonesia's Islamic finance ecosystem (Sharia-compliant banking, takaful insurance, sukuk markets, Islamic funds).
aIDZQDIBP.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.

aIDZIDIBP.description: IFDI, Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Islamic Banks & Windows
aIDZIDIBP.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator (IFDI): Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Islamic Banks & Windows. Reference data on Indonesia's Islamic finance ecosystem (Sharia-compliant banking, takaful insurance, sukuk markets, Islamic funds).
aIDZIDIBP.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.

aIDZADIBP.description: IFDI, Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Publicly Listed Islamic Banks
aIDZADIBP.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator (IFDI): Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Publicly Listed Islamic Banks. Reference data on Indonesia's Islamic finance ecosystem (Sharia-compliant banking, takaful insurance, sukuk markets, Islamic funds).
aIDZADIBP.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.

aIDZODIBR.description: IFDI, Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Return on Assets
aIDZODIBR.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator (IFDI): Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Return on Assets. Reference data on Indonesia's Islamic finance ecosystem (Sharia-compliant banking, takaful insurance, sukuk markets, Islamic funds).
aIDZODIBR.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.

aIDZODIBP.description: IFDI, Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Windows
aIDZODIBP.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator (IFDI): Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Windows. Reference data on Indonesia's Islamic finance ecosystem (Sharia-compliant banking, takaful insurance, sukuk markets, Islamic funds).
aIDZODIBP.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.

aIDZQDTKA.description: IFDI, Financial Performance, Takaful & Retakaful, Assets
aIDZQDTKA.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator (IFDI): Financial Performance, Takaful & Retakaful, Assets. Reference data on Indonesia's Islamic finance ecosystem (Sharia-compliant banking, takaful insurance, sukuk markets, Islamic funds).
aIDZQDTKA.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.

aIDASSTOT.meaning: Bank Indonesia: total assets — the central bank balance sheet asset side. Includes FX reserves (largest component, ~80%), claims on government, claims on banks, and other domestic assets.
aIDASSTOT.how_to_use: Tracks BI's monetary expansion. FX assets dominate — moves with reserve accumulation/intervention. Domestic asset growth (claims on government, claims on banks) reflects unconventional easing or liquidity provision. 2020 COVID saw unprecedented BI bond purchases under burden-sharing arrangements.

aIDLIABT.meaning: Bank Indonesia: total liabilities — currency in circulation, bank reserve deposits, government deposits, BI Certificates (SBI), and BI bills (SDBI).
aIDLIABT.how_to_use: Mirror of total assets by accounting identity. Currency in circulation is the largest stable component; bank reserves at BI absorb daily liquidity fluctuations. SBI/SDBI issuance is BI's main sterilization tool — rising stock indicates BI absorbing excess system liquidity.

aIDESECOP.description: Indonesia, EMISSIONS - CARBON DIOXIDE, Volume, Commodity Fundamentals, Annual, British Petroleum
aIDESECOP.meaning: Indonesia, Emissions — Carbon Dioxide — annual CO2 emissions volume. Indonesia is the world's ~10th largest emitter, with significant share from deforestation + coal power.
aIDESECOP.how_to_use: Tracks emissions trajectory under Indonesia's NDC (Nationally Determined Contributions) commitments. Net-zero target 2060. Coal-power phase-out is the major decarbonization variable.

aIDCRDCONAA.description: Commercial banks. outstanding credits to individuals, in rupiah
aIDCRDCONAA.meaning: Outstanding credits of commercial banks to individuals (in rupiah) — total household debt at banks. Includes mortgages, vehicle loans, multipurpose loans, credit cards.
aIDCRDCONAA.how_to_use: Indonesia's household debt is low by international standards (~17% of GDP vs 50-100% for DM). Mortgages dominate (~40% of household credit), followed by multipurpose loans, vehicle loans, credit cards. Household-credit-to-GDP rising signals deepening financial inclusion — generally positive but watch for excess.

aIDLOBHH.description: Outstanding credits of commercial banks, housing
aIDLOBHH.meaning: Outstanding Housing Credits at commercial banks — KPR (Kredit Pemilikan Rumah) mortgages. The largest single household credit category.
aIDLOBHH.how_to_use: Indonesia mortgage market is small but growing — mortgage-to-GDP ~3% (vs 30-60% for DM). Highly rate-sensitive: surge in BI cuts drives KPR demand. OJK macroprudential tools include mortgage LTV caps (currently 80-90% for first home, lower for second/third).

aIDGPCP/C.meaning: Final Consumption Expenditure, Private — household + NPISH (non-profit institutions) consumption in constant prices.
aIDGPCP/C.how_to_use: Tracks household + non-profit final consumption. Slightly broader than household-only consumption (aIDCPCED/CA).

aIDGPCG.description: Final Consumption Expenditure, General Government, Current Prices, Consumption, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDGPCG.meaning: Final Consumption Expenditure, General Government, Current Prices — nominal government consumption.
aIDGPCG.how_to_use: Use real version for cycle analysis; nominal for fiscal arithmetic.

aIDCNGOVR/C.meaning: Government Spending (Constant Prices) — government final consumption expenditure in real terms. Same concept as aIDCGCED/CA.
aIDCNGOVR/C.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use either for government-spending volume tracking.

aIDEMPAFNF.meaning: Employment in Agriculture, Forestry, Hunting & Fishery — workers in primary sectors. ~28% of total employment but only ~13% of GDP.
aIDEMPAFNF.how_to_use: Productivity-gap measure: employment share much higher than GDP share signals low-productivity informal-rural employment. Structural decline from ~40% (2010) to ~28% (2024) reflects urbanization.

aIDEMPLMT.meaning: Employment, Annual Total — BPS annual labor-force employment level. Aggregate of formal + informal sector employed.
aIDEMPLMT.how_to_use: Indonesia total employment ~135-140M. Annual frequency cleaner for trend. Watch for capacity-utilization signals: sustained employment gains alongside flat output point to labor-productivity headwinds.

aIDEMPSNPS.meaning: Employment in Community, Social & Personal Services — workers in education, healthcare, government services, household services.
aIDEMPSNPS.how_to_use: Stable, counter-cyclical category. Government employment dominates (civil servants, teachers, healthcare workers). Public-sector hiring decisions drive trend.

aIDEMPC.meaning: Employment in Construction — workers employed in residential, commercial, infrastructure construction. ~7% of total employment.
aIDEMPC.how_to_use: Highly cyclical with infrastructure spending and BI rates. Surged during 2014-2024 infrastructure push; decelerated since. Watch alongside cement consumption.

aIDEMEGNWS.meaning: Employment in Electricity, Gas & Water — utility-sector workers. Small share (<1%) but high productivity.
aIDEMEGNWS.how_to_use: Stable, low-cyclicality. Tracks state-owned utility (PLN) employment patterns plus IPP (independent power producer) staffing.

aIDEBIFINRE.description: Employment, Financing, insurance, real estate, business service
aIDEBIFINRE.meaning: Employment in Financing, Insurance, Real Estate, Business Services — white-collar professional employment.
aIDEBIFINRE.how_to_use: Indicator of services-economy maturation. Tracks bank, insurance, asset-management, professional-services hiring. Concentrated in Jakarta/major cities.

aIDEMPMF.meaning: Employment in Manufacturing — workers employed in the manufacturing sector. ~14% of total employment but ~20% of GDP.
aIDEMPMF.how_to_use: Track for manufacturing-cycle signal. Sustained declines flag deindustrialization concerns. Pair with manufacturing GVA (aIDVADGM/C) for productivity calculations.

aIDEMPMNQ.meaning: Employment in Mining and Quarrying — workers in extractive industries. Small employment share (~1.5%) but high productivity.
aIDEMPMNQ.how_to_use: Cyclical with commodity prices. Track for major mine closures/openings (Freeport's Grasberg expansion, Newmont/Amman's Batu Hijau). High average wages drive disproportionate income contribution.

aIDEMTOTOP.meaning: Employment, Quarterly Total — higher-frequency BPS employment release. Captures total employed across sectors.
aIDEMTOTOP.how_to_use: Use for cyclical tracking between annual Sakernas releases. Quarterly volatility from agricultural seasonality (planting/harvest cycles) is high.

aIDEMPTSC.meaning: Employment in Transportation, Storage & Communications — workers in logistics, transport, telecom, ICT services.
aIDEMPTSC.how_to_use: Growing share post-2015 with digital economy expansion (Gojek, Grab drivers). E-commerce + ride-hailing have created new employment categories captured here.

aIDWSNHNR.description: Employment, Wholesale & retail trade, restaurants, hotels
aIDWSNHNR.meaning: Employment in Wholesale & Retail Trade, Restaurants, Hotels — distributive trades + tourism employment. ~22% of total.
aIDWSNHNR.how_to_use: Second-largest employment sector after agriculture. Cyclical with consumer spending and tourism flows. Pair with retail sales (aIDRSLSAR) for the distributive-trades cycle.

aIDWKUNTTP.meaning: Labour Force, Unemployment — total unemployed persons in the labor force. Number of people without work but actively seeking.
aIDWKUNTTP.how_to_use: Combine with employment count to compute unemployment rate. Indonesia ~7-8M unemployed (2024) out of ~143M labor force.

aIDCEMPO/A.description: Employment, Employment, Payroll jobs, Standardized (based on source annual data)
aIDCEMPO/A.meaning: Employment, Payroll Jobs (Standardized) — formal-sector employment level. From BPS Sakernas (Labor Force Survey).
aIDCEMPO/A.how_to_use: Indonesia formal-sector employment ~50-55M people; informal sector ~80M. Formal-share growth signals labor-market modernization. Track YoY pace for cyclical signal.

aIDBISNXBR.description: BIS, Nominal Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index
aIDBISNXBR.meaning: BIS Nominal Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index for IDR — trade-weighted IDR vs basket of trading partners' currencies, in nominal terms. Compiled by the Bank for International Settlements; rebased to 100.
aIDBISNXBR.how_to_use: Better than IDR/USD alone for tracking IDR competitiveness — captures moves vs CNY, JPY, EUR, AUD, MYR, SGD (Indonesia's main trade partners). Falling NEER = IDR weakening on a trade-weighted basis. Use alongside the real EER (aIDBISRXBR) for inflation-adjusted competitiveness.

aIDBISRXBR.description: BIS, Real Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index
aIDBISRXBR.meaning: BIS Real Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index for IDR — trade-weighted IDR adjusted for relative inflation against trading partners. The 'true' competitiveness gauge.
aIDBISRXBR.how_to_use: Most analytically meaningful FX gauge. Rising real EER = IDR getting more expensive in real terms = exports become less competitive. Indonesia's real EER stayed elevated 2010-2014 (commodity supercycle) then weakened post-2015 — supporting the trade balance recovery. Watch for sustained real EER appreciation as a current-account deterioration signal.

aIDOCFPP/A.description: Purchasing power parity, National currency per USD
aIDOCFPP/A.meaning: Purchasing Power Parity, National currency per USD — same conceptual measure as aIDOAPPPGR.
aIDOCFPP/A.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use either for cross-country price-level comparisons.

aIDXRUSD.meaning: Indonesian Rupiah per US Dollar — the headline IDR/USD spot rate. Daily fixing published by Bank Indonesia (Jakarta Interbank Spot Dollar Rate, JISDOR) around 10:00 WIB.
aIDXRUSD.how_to_use: THE Indonesia FX rate. Recent range: 14,500-16,800. Sustained moves above 16,500 typically trigger BI verbal then physical intervention (FX sales from reserves). DXY (broad USD index) and EM risk sentiment dominate near-term moves; commodity prices (coal, palm oil) and current account balance drive the trend. Pair with aIDCRESA (FX reserves) — sustained reserve drawdowns alongside IDR weakness signal stressed defense.

aIDFFXDB.meaning: External Debt: Banks — Indonesian banks' foreign-currency borrowings (interbank lines, syndications, FX bonds).
aIDFFXDB.how_to_use: ~$50B. Banks fund their FX loan books via FX deposits + external borrowing. Watch for sudden surges as a sign of dollar funding squeezes. Indonesian regulator (OJK) caps banks' foreign-currency net open positions to limit FX risk.

aIDFFEDLGOV.meaning: External Debt: General Government — the central + sub-national government foreign debt component. Closely tracks aIDCGVXA with minor methodological differences.
aIDFFEDLGOV.how_to_use: Use for cross-validation against aIDCGVXA. The 'general government' framing aligns with IMF/SDDS reporting standards. Sub-national (provincial, regency) external debt is small in Indonesia — central government dominates.

aIDFFXDMA.meaning: External Debt: Monetary Authorities — Bank Indonesia's foreign liabilities (IMF SDR allocation, FX swap lines, etc.).
aIDFFXDMA.how_to_use: Small. Includes BI's bilateral swap lines (with PBOC, BoJ, etc.) and IMF allocations. Activated swaps appear here.

aIDFFXDOTS.meaning: External Debt: Other Sectors — non-financial corporate external debt. Includes USD/EUR bonds issued by SOEs (Pertamina, PLN) and private corporates, plus offshore loans.
aIDFFXDOTS.how_to_use: ~$200B. State-owned enterprises (PLN, Pertamina) account for a large share — their FX bonds are quasi-sovereign. Watch corporate refinancing schedules around major maturities; FX-mismatched corporates are the EM-stress vulnerability point.

aIDDEBTFT.meaning: External Debt, Total (SDDS-sourced) — IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard external-debt total.
aIDDEBTFT.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCEXTA. SDDS-format aligns with international debt-statistics standards.

aIDCGVXPA.description: Government External Debt, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCGVXPA.meaning: Government External Debt, QoQ absolute change — change in government foreign debt level.
aIDCGVXPA.how_to_use: Tracks Treasury's foreign-currency funding cadence. Indonesia's typical pattern: USD/EUR/JPY bond issuance front-loaded in Q1.

aIDCGVXYA.description: Government External Debt, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCGVXYA.meaning: Government External Debt, YoY change — pace of government external-borrowing growth.
aIDCGVXYA.how_to_use: Track for sovereign-financing cycle. Indonesia gov external debt YoY growth typically 5-10%; surges during fiscal-stress years (2020 COVID).

aIDCGVXA.meaning: Government External Debt — central government's foreign-currency debt + non-resident-held SBN. Largest single component of total external debt.
aIDCGVXA.how_to_use: Indonesia government external debt ~$200B. Decompose: bilateral/multilateral loans (~$50B, mostly USD/JPY) + global bonds (~$80B in USD, EUR, JPY, samurai) + non-resident SBN holdings (~$70B). Foreign-currency portion is the FX-risk concern; non-resident SBN is the flow-risk concern (sudden outflows).

aIDCEXTPA.description: Total External Debt, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCEXTPA.meaning: Total External Debt, QoQ absolute change — change in external debt level vs prior quarter.
aIDCEXTPA.how_to_use: Track for borrowing cycle. Sharp QoQ surges (>$10B) signal aggressive external borrowing.

aIDCEXTYA.description: Total External Debt, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCEXTYA.meaning: Total External Debt, year-over-year change — pace of external-debt accumulation or paydown.
aIDCEXTYA.how_to_use: Track for external-vulnerability buildup. Sustained >10% YoY growth signals over-borrowing in foreign currency. Indonesia ran 8-12% YoY growth pre-COVID (driven by infrastructure financing); recent growth slower (~3-5%). Spike in YoY rate alongside IDR weakness flags refinancing stress.

aIDCEXTA.meaning: Total External Debt — debt owed to non-residents in foreign currencies + IDR-denominated debt held by foreigners. Published quarterly by Bank Indonesia (SULNI report).
aIDCEXTA.how_to_use: Indonesia's external debt ~$415B (2024). Composition: ~50% government, ~25% banks, ~25% non-financial corporates. Compare to FX reserves (~$140B) and exports (~$300B) for adequacy gauges. External debt to GDP ~30% — moderate but rising.

aIDEAEXP.meaning: Exports of Goods and Services — alternative framing of export aggregate. Released alongside foreign-transaction statistics.
aIDEAEXP.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCEXBA (BoP) and aIDCEXPB/A (BPS monthly trade). Methodology differences are minor.

aIDEAIMP.meaning: Imports of Goods and Services — alternative framing of import aggregate.
aIDEAIMP.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCIMBA (BoP) and aIDCIMPB/A (BPS monthly trade).

aIDGDYMPRR.description: Chg Y/Y, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDGDYMPRR.meaning: GDP/GVA by Industry, YoY — aggregate measure of value-added growth across industry sectors. Companion to GDP-by-expenditure release.
aIDGDYMPRR.how_to_use: Should track aIDCGDPYD/A closely. Differences reflect statistical-discrepancy items between expenditure and production approaches to GDP.

aIDVAEAHOTE/C.description: GDP - ACCOMMODATION & FOOD SERVICE ACTIVITIES, Constant Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVAEAHOTE/C.meaning: GDP — Accommodation & Food Service Activities, Constant Prices — real hotels + restaurants GVA.
aIDVAEAHOTE/C.how_to_use: Pre-COVID growth ~6% pa; collapsed in 2020-21; recovering. Tracks Bali tourism + middle-class restaurant spending.

aIDVAEAHOTE.description: GDP - ACCOMMODATION & FOOD SERVICE ACTIVITIES, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVAEAHOTE.meaning: GDP — Accommodation & Food Service Activities, Current Prices — hotels + restaurants nominal GVA. ~2.5% of GDP.
aIDVAEAHOTE.how_to_use: Use constant-prices version (aIDVAEAHOTE/C) for volume cycle. Tracks tourism + domestic-restaurant demand.

aIDEAAG/C.description: GDP - AGRICULTURE, FORESTRY & FISHING, Constant Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDEAAG/C.meaning: GDP — Agriculture, Forestry & Fishing, constant prices. Includes palm oil, rubber, rice, fisheries. ~13% of GDP and ~28% of employment (high share given low productivity).
aIDEAAG/C.how_to_use: Important for rural incomes and food prices. Palm oil exports (Indonesia is world's largest producer with Malaysia) drive value-added swings. Weather (El Niño, La Niña) is the dominant short-term variable. Pair with food CPI for the rural-urban transmission signal.

aIDEAAG.description: GDP - AGRICULTURE, FORESTRY & FISHING, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDEAAG.meaning: GDP — Agriculture, Forestry & Fishing, Current Prices — nominal value-added in agriculture sector. Companion to aIDEAAG/C (constant prices).
aIDEAAG.how_to_use: Use constant-prices version for cycle analysis; nominal version for nominal-GDP composition. Indonesia agri sector ~13% of nominal GDP, dominated by palm oil + rice + fisheries.

aIDVADELWAT/C.description: GDP - ELECTRICITY & GAS SUPPLY, Constant Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADELWAT/C.meaning: GDP — Electricity & Gas Supply, Constant Prices — real utilities GVA. ~1.2% of GDP.
aIDVADELWAT/C.how_to_use: Stable growth ~5% pa tracks GDP. Electricity demand growth a development indicator.

aIDVADELWAT.description: GDP - ELECTRICITY & GAS SUPPLY, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADELWAT.meaning: GDP — Electricity & Gas Supply, Current Prices — nominal utilities sector GVA. Includes PLN (state electricity utility) and gas distribution.
aIDVADELWAT.how_to_use: Stable, low-cyclicality. Tracks electrification and economic growth.

aIDVAFONBS/C.description: GDP - FINANCIAL & INSURANCE ACTIVITIES, Constant Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVAFONBS/C.meaning: GDP — Financial & Insurance Activities, constant prices — bank, insurance, asset-management sector value added. ~4% of GDP, smaller than DM economies (10-15%) but growing.
aIDVAFONBS/C.how_to_use: Tracks financialization of the economy. Bank profitability cycles, insurance penetration (still very low at ~3% of GDP — major growth opportunity), and capital markets development drive growth. Indonesia's domestic capital markets remain underdeveloped vs peers — finance-sector GDP share is a structural-development metric.

aIDVAFONBS.description: GDP - FINANCIAL & INSURANCE ACTIVITIES, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVAFONBS.meaning: GDP — Financial & Insurance Activities, Current Prices — nominal finance-sector GVA.
aIDVAFONBS.how_to_use: Use constant-prices version (aIDVAFONBS/C) for cycle. ~4% of GDP.

aIDVADSS/C.description: GDP - OTHER SERVICES ACTIVITIES, Constant Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADSS/C.meaning: GDP — Other Services Activities, Constant Prices — real residual services GVA. Small share (~2%).
aIDVADSS/C.how_to_use: Captures non-categorized services. Use category-specific GVA series for sector cycle analysis.

aIDVADSS.description: GDP - OTHER SERVICES ACTIVITIES, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADSS.meaning: GDP — Other Services Activities, Current Prices — nominal residual services GVA. Includes personal services, household services, NGO activities.
aIDVADSS.how_to_use: Use constant-prices version (aIDVADSS/C) for volume cycle. Captures services not classified in main sectors. Small share of GDP (~2%).

aIDVAEATRAC/C.description: GDP - TRANSPORTATION & STORAGE, Constant Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVAEATRAC/C.meaning: GDP — Transportation & Storage, constant prices. Includes road, rail, air, sea transport plus warehousing. ~5% of GDP. Vital for an archipelagic economy.
aIDVAEATRAC/C.how_to_use: Logistics costs are a long-running competitiveness drag — Indonesia logistics-cost-to-GDP runs ~24% (vs ~14% for ASEAN-5 peers). Toll-road network expansion and Pelabuhan Indonesia (port operator) mergers aim to reduce this. Sector growth correlates with manufacturing and trade volumes.

aIDVAEATRAC.description: GDP - TRANSPORTATION & STORAGE, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVAEATRAC.meaning: GDP — Transportation & Storage, Current Prices — nominal transport-and-storage GVA.
aIDVAEATRAC.how_to_use: Use constant-prices version (aIDVAEATRAC/C). ~5% of GDP. Critical for archipelagic economy.

aIDCNHNPIA.description: NPI SERVING HOUSEHOLD CONSUMPTION EXPENDITURE, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDCNHNPIA.meaning: NPI Serving Household Consumption Expenditure, Current Prices — final consumption expenditure of non-profit institutions serving households (NPISH). Small GDP component (~1%).
aIDCNHNPIA.how_to_use: Niche. Niches captures religious organizations, charities, foundations. Tracks NGO and faith-organization activity.

aIDVADCONS/C.description: Value Added, Economic Activity, Construction, Constant Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADCONS/C.meaning: Value Added: Construction, constant prices — construction sector GDP. Includes infrastructure (roads, ports, railways), residential, and commercial real estate construction. ~11% of GDP.
aIDVADCONS/C.how_to_use: Highly cyclical with infrastructure spending and BI rates. Surged during Jokowi's 2014-2024 infrastructure push (toll roads, MRT, dams, airports). Deceleration since 2024 reflects rate hikes and fiscal consolidation. Track alongside cement consumption and steel demand.

aIDVADCONS.description: Value Added, Economic Activity, Construction, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADCONS.meaning: Value Added: Construction, Current Prices — nominal construction sector GVA.
aIDVADCONS.how_to_use: Use constant-prices version (aIDVADCONS/C) for volume cycle. ~11% of nominal GDP.

aIDVADGM/C.description: Value Added, Economic Activity, Manufacturing industry, Constant Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADGM/C.meaning: Value Added: Manufacturing Industry, constant prices — the manufacturing sector's contribution to GDP at constant prices. Indonesia's largest single industry sector at ~18-20% of GDP.
aIDVADGM/C.how_to_use: Indonesia targets manufacturing as a growth driver (Making Indonesia 4.0 program). Key sub-sectors: food & beverage (largest), chemicals, transportation equipment, base metals (nickel processing post-2020 export bans). Track quarterly growth — sustained sub-3% indicates deindustrialization concerns.

aIDVADGM.description: Value Added, Economic Activity, Manufacturing industry, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADGM.meaning: Value Added: Manufacturing Industry, Current Prices — nominal manufacturing GVA.
aIDVADGM.how_to_use: Use constant-prices version (aIDVADGM/C) for cycle. Manufacturing is Indonesia's largest single sector at ~18-20% of nominal GDP.

aIDVADMIN/C.description: Value Added, Economic Activity, Mining and quarrying, Constant Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADMIN/C.meaning: Value Added: Mining and Quarrying, constant prices — the mining/extractive sector's contribution to GDP. Includes coal, oil/gas, nickel, copper, gold, tin extraction. ~10-12% of GDP, highly cyclical with commodity prices.
aIDVADMIN/C.how_to_use: Most volatile GDP component. Coal (Indonesia is world's largest thermal coal exporter) and oil/gas dominate. Surged 2021-22 with commodity boom; decelerated 2023+ on lower coal/nickel prices. Watch global commodity prices for the leading signal.

aIDVADMIN.description: Value Added, Economic Activity, Mining and quarrying, Current Prices, GDP/GVA by Industry, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDVADMIN.meaning: Value Added: Mining and Quarrying, Current Prices — nominal mining sector GVA.
aIDVADMIN.how_to_use: Highly volatile with commodity prices. Use constant-prices version (aIDVADMIN/C) for volume cycle.

aIDGDPYAR.description: Chg Y/Y, GDP by Expenditure, Annual, Statistics Indonesia
aIDGDPYAR.meaning: GDP YoY (Annual, BPS) — annualized GDP growth from BPS annual release.
aIDGDPYAR.how_to_use: Long-time-series annual frequency complement to quarterly. Use for multi-year trend assessment.

aIDGDPAR.description: GDP, Annualized growth rate, Chg Y/Y
aIDGDPAR.meaning: GDP Annualized Growth Rate — alternative framing of GDP YoY. Reuters poll-anchored series used as forecast benchmark.
aIDGDPAR.how_to_use: Used by markets as expectations anchor before BPS quarterly release. Comparison vs actual print drives IDR + SBN yields same-day.

aIDGDPXCAL.meaning: GDP, Chg P/P — period-on-period growth rate of GDP. Same conceptual measure as aIDCGDPPD/A in a different framing.
aIDGDPXCAL.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use either for sequential momentum tracking.

aIDGDP/C.description: GDP, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDGDP/C.meaning: GDP at Constant Prices (BPS quarterly) — alternative release of real GDP level. Same conceptual measure as aIDCGDPD/CA from a different vintage.
aIDGDP/C.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data. Real GDP is the meaningful growth signal.

aIDGDPCUR.description: GDP, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDGDPCUR.meaning: GDP at Current Prices (BPS quarterly) — alternative release of nominal GDP level. Same as aIDCGDPA from a different vintage.
aIDGDPCUR.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCGDPA. Use for nominal-GDP analysis (debt/GDP, deficit/GDP ratios).

aIDGDPQAR.meaning: GDP Actual QoQ — Reuters poll-anchored release of GDP quarter-over-quarter growth.
aIDGDPQAR.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCGDPPD/A. Markets watch QoQ alongside YoY but YoY remains the headline for Indonesia.

aIDGDPAR1.meaning: GDP Actual YoY — Reuters poll-anchored 'actual' release of GDP year-over-year growth. Used in forecast-vs-actual comparisons.
aIDGDPAR1.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCGDPYD/A. Reuters polls Indonesia's chief economists ahead of release; the 'actual' is set when BPS publishes.

aIDCEXNPD/A.description: Exports - Goods & Services, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCEXNPD/A.meaning: Exports of Goods and Services, QoQ percent change in constant prices — sequential export-volume momentum.
aIDCEXNPD/A.how_to_use: Volatile quarterly. Smooth with 4-quarter moving average. Use YoY (aIDCEXNYD/A) for trend.

aIDCEXNYD/A.description: Exports - Goods & Services, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCEXNYD/A.meaning: Exports of Goods and Services, year-over-year change in constant prices. Captures both merchandise and services exports in real terms.
aIDCEXNYD/A.how_to_use: Highly correlated with global commodity prices — Indonesia's top exports are coal, palm oil, nickel, oil/gas, and manufactures. China is the largest single export market (~25%). Watch CNY weakness and China industrial demand for the leading signal. Surge in export growth (>15% YoY) typically coincides with commodity cycle peaks.
