aIDCEXND/CA.meaning: Exports of Goods and Services — constant-price level. Volume measure of external demand for Indonesia's output.
aIDCEXND/CA.how_to_use: Use for export-volume tracking distinct from price-driven nominal swings. Volume-vs-price decomposition tells you whether export strength is commodity-price-driven or genuinely volume-driven.

aIDCGPPPD/CA.description: GDP based on Purchasing Power Parity, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/LSEG
aIDCGPPPD/CA.meaning: GDP PPP, QoQ growth in constant prices — companion to aIDCGPPPNA.
aIDCGPPPD/CA.how_to_use: Use real GDP QoQ (aIDCGDPPD/A) for analytical purposes; PPP versions for cross-country comparison.

aIDCGPPPNA.description: GDP based on Purchasing Power Parity, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/LSEG
aIDCGPPPNA.meaning: GDP PPP, QoQ change — sequential momentum of PPP-adjusted GDP.
aIDCGPPPNA.how_to_use: Less commonly used than YoY. PPP conversion factors are static within a year so QoQ should track real-GDP QoQ closely.

aIDCGPPYB/CA.description: GDP based on Purchasing Power Parity, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/LSEG
aIDCGPPYB/CA.meaning: GDP based on PPP, year-over-year change in constant prices — real PPP-GDP growth rate.
aIDCGPPYB/CA.how_to_use: Should track aIDCGDPYD/A closely (PPP growth ≈ real-GDP growth). Differences arise from PPP-conversion-factor revisions in IMF benchmark studies.

aIDCGPPYEA.description: GDP based on Purchasing Power Parity, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/LSEG
aIDCGPPYEA.meaning: GDP based on PPP, YoY change (alternate release) — real PPP-adjusted GDP year-over-year growth.
aIDCGPPYEA.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCGPPYB/CA. Should track real-GDP YoY closely.

aIDCGPPWN/CA.description: GDP based on Purchasing Power Parity, Standardized, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/LSEG
aIDCGPPWN/CA.meaning: GDP based on Purchasing Power Parity, constant prices — real PPP-adjusted GDP level. Used for long-run comparisons across countries.
aIDCGPPWN/CA.how_to_use: Track Indonesia's relative weight in world output. Indonesia's share of global PPP GDP has risen from ~2% (2000) to ~3% (2024).

aIDCGPPOGA.description: GDP based on Purchasing Power Parity, Standardized, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/LSEG
aIDCGPPOGA.meaning: GDP based on Purchasing Power Parity, current prices — IMF-compiled PPP-adjusted GDP. Adjusts for cross-country price-level differences.
aIDCGPPOGA.how_to_use: Indonesia PPP GDP ~$4.5 trillion (2024) — world's 7th largest economy by PPP, ahead of UK and France. Use PPP for relative-economic-size comparisons; current-USD GDP for trade-weight comparisons.

aIDCGDPEX/C.description: GDP, Standardized, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Annual, Statistics Indonesia/LSEG
aIDCGDPEX/C.meaning: GDP at constant prices, annual — same conceptual measure as aIDCGDPD/CA at annual frequency. Used for long-time-series analysis.
aIDCGDPEX/C.how_to_use: Use for multi-year trend analysis. Annual frequency cleaner for spotting structural slowdowns (e.g., the 2014-2016 commodity-bust deceleration from 6%+ to ~5% trend growth).

aIDCIMNPD/A.description: Imports - Goods & Services, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCIMNPD/A.meaning: Imports of Goods and Services, QoQ percent change in constant prices — sequential import-volume momentum.
aIDCIMNPD/A.how_to_use: Pro-cyclical with domestic demand. Volatile quarterly; use YoY for trend.

aIDCIMNYD/A.description: Imports - Goods & Services, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCIMNYD/A.meaning: Imports of Goods and Services, year-over-year change in constant prices. Captures both merchandise and services imports in real terms.
aIDCIMNYD/A.how_to_use: Pro-cyclical with domestic demand and capital investment (capital goods imports rise with GFCF). Falls in IDR weakness episodes due to import cost pass-through (oil products, capital goods). When import growth exceeds export growth for sustained periods, watch the current account for deficit deterioration.

aIDCIMND/CA.meaning: Imports of Goods and Services — constant-price level. Volume measure of import demand.
aIDCIMND/CA.how_to_use: Use to separate volume-driven import dynamics from price effects. Capital goods volume leads investment by 1-2 quarters.

aIDCPCEPD/A.description: Consumer Spending, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCPCEPD/A.meaning: Consumer Spending, QoQ percent change in constant prices — sequential consumption momentum.
aIDCPCEPD/A.how_to_use: Volatile (Lebaran-Eid timing dominates Q2/Q3 swings). Use YoY for trend; QoQ for revisions and inflection signals.

aIDCPCEYD/A.description: Consumer Spending, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCPCEYD/A.meaning: Household Consumption Expenditure, year-over-year change in constant prices. Largest component of Indonesia GDP at ~55%. Includes goods + services purchased by households.
aIDCPCEYD/A.how_to_use: Drives ~55% of GDP — the most important growth component. Track around major holidays: Lebaran (Eid al-Fitr) typically lifts Q2 or Q3 consumption depending on calendar; Christmas/New Year boosts Q4. Sustained sub-4% household consumption growth signals weak domestic demand and Bank Indonesia easing pressure. Pair with consumer confidence (aIDCONCF) and retail sales.

aIDCPCED/CA.meaning: Consumer Spending (Household Final Consumption) — constant-price level. The largest GDP component (~55%).
aIDCPCED/CA.how_to_use: Use the level for analytical baseline; YoY (aIDCPCEYD/A) is the meaningful growth signal. Indonesia's consumption-led growth model means household spending dynamics dominate.

aIDCGDHD/CA.description: GDP per capita, Constant prices, Standardized (based on annual data)
aIDCGDHD/CA.meaning: GDP per capita, constant prices, standardized — real income per person. Most analytically meaningful per-capita measure for tracking living standards over time.
aIDCGDHD/CA.how_to_use: Indonesia is in the middle-income trap conversation: per-capita PPP GDP ~US$15,000 (2024). Annual real growth ~3-4% per capita reflects population growth (~1% pa) subtracted from GDP growth (~5%). Track for long-term convergence narrative — Indonesia targeted high-income status by 2045.

aIDCYDHD/CA.description: GDP per capita, Constant prices, Standardized.
aIDCYDHD/CA.meaning: GDP per capita, constant prices, standardized — same conceptual measure as aIDCGDHD/CA at standardized framing.
aIDCYDHD/CA.how_to_use: Use for international comparison. Domestic analysts use aIDCGDHD/CA. Real per-capita growth ~3-4% pa in Indonesia (5% GDP minus 1% population).

aIDCGDHQA.description: GDP per capita, Current prices, Standardized
aIDCGDHQA.meaning: GDP per capita, current prices, quarterly — nominal per-capita GDP at higher frequency.
aIDCGDHQA.how_to_use: Use annual (aIDCGDHA) for level comparisons; quarterly for tracking trend acceleration. Population assumptions (BPS census) drive denominator.

aIDCGDHA.description: GDP per capita, Current prices, Standardized (based on annual data)
aIDCGDHA.meaning: GDP per capita, current prices, annual — nominal GDP per person. Used for income-level benchmarking.
aIDCGDHA.how_to_use: Indonesia per-capita GDP (current prices) ~Rp 75 million (~$5,000 USD) in 2024. Watch for milestone crossings — passing $7,000 per capita typically marks middle-income middle-stage transition.

aIDCGDPPD/A.description: GDP, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/Refinitiv
aIDCGDPPD/A.meaning: Real GDP growth, quarter-over-quarter change in constant prices — the higher-frequency complement to YoY. Indonesia GDP is highly seasonal (Lebaran-Eid timing affects Q2/Q3 mix), so QoQ is reported but YoY is the more market-relevant signal.
aIDCGDPPD/A.how_to_use: Use for sequential momentum. Indonesia's QoQ pattern is highly seasonal — Q1 typically negative (post-holiday wind-down), Q3 positive (Lebaran spending if it falls in Q3). Focus on YoY (aIDCGDPYD/A) for trend; QoQ for revisions and sequential acceleration/deceleration.

aIDCGDPPA.description: GDP, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/Refinitiv
aIDCGDPPA.meaning: GDP at current prices, quarter-over-quarter percent change — nominal GDP growth pace. Combines real growth + GDP deflator (inflation).
aIDCGDPPA.how_to_use: Used in fiscal arithmetic (debt/GDP and deficit/GDP move with nominal GDP). Compare to real QoQ (aIDCGDPPD/A) — the gap is GDP-deflator inflation. Recent nominal QoQ runs ~3-4% reflecting ~1% real + ~2% deflator.

aIDCGDPYD/A.description: GDP, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/Refinitiv
aIDCGDPYD/A.meaning: Real GDP growth, year-over-year change in constant prices — the headline Indonesia growth print. Released quarterly by BPS-Statistics Indonesia (Badan Pusat Statistik) with a ~6-week lag (e.g., Q1 data published in early May).
aIDCGDPYD/A.how_to_use: THE Indonesia growth number markets watch. Trend ~5% per year is the post-2014 norm — Indonesia hasn't seen recession since 1998 Asian crisis (briefly negative in 2020 COVID). Sustained sub-4% prints raise concerns about structural slowdown; >5.5% suggests above-trend (often consumption-driven). Compare to consensus (Bloomberg/Reuters poll) — surprise drives IDR, SBN yields, and JCI.

aIDCGDPYA.description: GDP, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/Refinitiv
aIDCGDPYA.meaning: GDP at current prices, year-over-year percent change — nominal GDP growth rate. Captures both real growth and GDP deflator inflation.
aIDCGDPYA.how_to_use: Most useful in fiscal-arithmetic context (when computing debt or deficit as % of nominal GDP). Markets watch real GDP YoY (aIDCGDPYD/A) for the headline. Recent nominal YoY ~8-9% (5% real + 3% deflator).

aIDCGDPD/CA.description: GDP, Standardized, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/Refinitiv
aIDCGDPD/CA.meaning: GDP at constant prices, quarterly — real GDP level (volume measure). Reference base year is updated periodically by BPS (currently 2010 base).
aIDCGDPD/CA.how_to_use: The 'real economy' size measure. Use for constant-price level tracking. YoY (aIDCGDPYD/A) and QoQ (aIDCGDPPD/A) growth rates from this series are the most-watched headline numbers.

aIDCGDPA.description: GDP, Standardized, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia/Refinitiv
aIDCGDPA.meaning: GDP at current prices, quarterly — nominal GDP level by expenditure approach. Released quarterly by BPS-Statistics Indonesia.
aIDCGDPA.how_to_use: Use for nominal-GDP level analysis (debt/GDP, deficit/GDP ratios). Compare to constant-price GDP (aIDCGDPD/CA) — gap reflects the GDP deflator, Indonesia's broadest inflation gauge. Recent annualized nominal GDP ~Rp 22,000 trillion (~$1.4 trillion USD).

aIDCGCEPD/A.description: Government Consumption, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCGCEPD/A.meaning: Government Consumption, QoQ percent change in constant prices — sequential government-spending momentum.
aIDCGCEPD/A.how_to_use: Volatile. Reflects budget-execution patterns: Q4 typically sees spending push to use up budget allocations. Smooth with 4Q average for trend.

aIDCGCEYD/A.description: Government Consumption, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCGCEYD/A.meaning: Government Consumption, year-over-year change in constant prices — central + regional government final consumption (salaries, goods/services purchased). ~8% of Indonesia GDP, smaller share than most G20 economies.
aIDCGCEYD/A.how_to_use: Generally less cyclical than household consumption. Election-cycle distortions: government spending tends to accelerate in election years (2014, 2019, 2024). Subsidy spending (energy, food) shows up in this line. Watch for fiscal stimulus periods (2020 COVID response saw government consumption surge while private fell).

aIDCGCED/CA.meaning: Government Consumption — constant-price level. Central + regional government final consumption (salaries, goods/services purchased).
aIDCGCED/CA.how_to_use: Use level for analytical baseline; YoY (aIDCGCEYD/A) for cyclical tracking. Government consumption surges in election years and during crisis-response periods (2020 COVID).

aIDCGFCPD/A.description: Gross Fixed Capital Investment, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCGFCPD/A.meaning: Gross Fixed Capital Investment, QoQ percent change in constant prices — sequential investment momentum.
aIDCGFCPD/A.how_to_use: Volatile. Fiscal year-end capex pushes inflate Q4. Use YoY (aIDCGFCYD/A) for trend identification.

aIDCGFCYD/A.description: Gross Fixed Capital Investment, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCGFCYD/A.meaning: Gross Fixed Capital Formation, year-over-year change in constant prices — investment spending on machinery, buildings, infrastructure. ~30% of Indonesia GDP.
aIDCGFCYD/A.how_to_use: The cycle-sensitive growth component. Surges with infrastructure programs (Jokowi's 2014-2024 infrastructure push drove 6-8% pa GFCF growth) and FDI cycles. Decelerates sharply when BI rates rise. Pair with PMA (foreign investment realization, BKPM data) and domestic credit growth — when both stall, GFCF lags by 2-3 quarters.

aIDCGFCD/CA.meaning: Gross Fixed Capital Formation — constant-price level. Investment in machinery, buildings, infrastructure. ~30% of GDP.
aIDCGFCD/CA.how_to_use: Use level for analytical baseline; YoY (aIDCGFCYD/A) for cyclical signal. Investment is the cycle-sensitive growth component — accelerates with infrastructure programs and FDI cycles.

aIDGDPDEF/A.meaning: Implicit Price Deflator — alternative framing of the GDP price deflator. Computed as (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100.
aIDGDPDEF/A.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCIPDE/CA. Use for trend tracking — broadest measure of inflation in the Indonesian economy.

aIDCIPDPE/A.description: GDP Price Deflator, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCIPDPE/A.meaning: GDP Price Deflator, QoQ percent change — sequential broadest-inflation measure.
aIDCIPDPE/A.how_to_use: Volatile quarterly due to commodity-price-induced terms-of-trade shifts. Use YoY (aIDCIPDYE/A) for trend.

aIDCIPDYE/A.description: GDP Price Deflator, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCIPDYE/A.meaning: GDP Price Deflator, year-over-year change — annual broadest-inflation rate.
aIDCIPDYE/A.how_to_use: Indonesia GDP deflator inflation typically 3-5% YoY (vs CPI 2-3%). Persistent gap reflects commodity-price pass-through to producer prices and capital-goods inflation. Track for understanding nominal-real GDP gap.

aIDCIPDE/CA.meaning: GDP Price Deflator — broadest measure of inflation in the Indonesian economy. Computed as (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100. Captures price changes across all final goods and services in GDP.
aIDCIPDE/CA.how_to_use: Broader than CPI (which covers consumer goods only). Includes capital goods, government services, exports. When deflator inflation runs above CPI, suggests broader cost pressures (capex, infrastructure). BI does not target deflator but watches for divergence.

aIDGOVBALA.meaning: Central Government Operations: deficit/surplus — the headline fiscal balance for Indonesia. Released monthly by the Ministry of Finance (Kemenkeu) as part of the APBN (state budget) realization report.
aIDGOVBALA.how_to_use: Indonesia ran budget surpluses in commodity-boom years (2005-2008) and persistent deficits since. Constitutional cap: deficit ≤3% of GDP (per the State Finance Law) — temporarily lifted to 6.4% in 2020-2022 for COVID response. Recent target ~2.3-2.7% deficit/GDP. Surprises drive SBN bond yields and IDR.

aIDEXPDT.meaning: Government Expenditures, total — central government spending. Major lines: subsidies (energy, food), interest payments, salaries, capital spending, social spending, transfers to regional governments (DAU/DAK).
aIDEXPDT.how_to_use: Energy subsidy line is the most volatile — surges with oil prices and IDR weakness (when fuel is sold below cost). Interest payments now ~16% of expenditure (rising rapidly with debt buildup). Capital spending discipline is a sovereign-credit strength.

aIDCGREV.meaning: Government Revenues, total — central government tax + non-tax receipts. Major components: income tax (~25%), VAT (~30%), customs/excise (~15%), non-tax revenue (oil/gas, SOE dividends, ~20%).
aIDCGREV.how_to_use: Cyclical with GDP and commodity prices (oil/gas non-tax revenue). Tax-to-GDP ratio ~10-11% — low by global standards (vs 15-20% for most EM). Indonesia's tax base broadening is a long-running fiscal narrative. Surge in revenues vs target drives IDR positive (lower issuance need).

aIDCGOVA.description: Central government Deficit/Surplus, Standardized (based on source annual data)
aIDCGOVA.meaning: Central Government Deficit/Surplus, standardized — OECD-comparable framing of the central government fiscal balance. Published as part of the Ministry of Finance's monthly APBN realization.
aIDCGOVA.how_to_use: Same conceptual measure as aIDGOVBALA in standardized framing. Use for cross-country fiscal comparisons. Indonesia's deficit/GDP has been disciplined relative to most EM peers — supportive of investment-grade credit ratings (Indonesia rated BBB by S&P/Fitch, Baa2 by Moody's).

aIDGEXP.meaning: Central government expenditures — alternate framing of the headline expenditure series. Same concept as aIDEXPDT.
aIDGEXP.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDEXPDT. Use either for level tracking; expenditure growth and composition shifts (subsidy vs capex vs salary) drive medium-term fiscal trajectory.

aIDGDEF.meaning: Government Expenditures, Balanced Budget — fiscal-balance framing. Indonesia's fiscal-rule basis pre-COVID was 'balanced budget over the cycle' with 3% deficit cap.
aIDGDEF.how_to_use: Use aIDGOVBALA/aIDCGOVA for the headline deficit/surplus. This series provides a complementary view from balanced-budget framework.

aIDGOVEXA.meaning: Government Expenditures, Current Total — current-spending portion of expenditures (excludes capex). Includes salaries, subsidies, transfers, interest.
aIDGOVEXA.how_to_use: Current spending dominates Indonesia government expenditure (~85%). Capex share has stagnated despite infrastructure rhetoric. Watch capex share for fiscal-quality signal.

aIDGFINSD.meaning: Government Financing, Surplus/Deficit — financing side of the fiscal balance (how the deficit gets funded: domestic/external borrowing, asset sales, etc.).
aIDGFINSD.how_to_use: Should mirror the fiscal balance with opposite sign. Decomposition into domestic SBN issuance + external borrowing + drawdowns of cash buffer informs SBN supply outlook.

aIDPDEBTA.meaning: Public Debt outstanding — total central government debt, including SBN (Surat Berharga Negara, Indonesian government securities) issued domestically and externally, plus loans from multilaterals (World Bank, ADB) and bilateral creditors.
aIDPDEBTA.how_to_use: Indonesia's gross debt level rose from ~Rp 4,500T in 2019 to ~Rp 8,000T post-COVID. Domestic SBN dominates (~65% of total) — important for FX-risk insulation. Foreign holding share of SBN (~14%) is the key external-vulnerability metric — sharp drops mean foreign outflows pressuring IDR.

aIDCDBTGUR.description: Public debt as a percentage of GDP, Standardized
aIDCDBTGUR.meaning: Public debt as a percentage of GDP — the standard sustainability gauge. Published quarterly by Ministry of Finance.
aIDCDBTGUR.how_to_use: Indonesia's debt/GDP rose from ~30% (pre-COVID) to ~40% (2024) — still moderate vs DM peers (90-130%) and EM peers like India (~85%) or Brazil (~85%). The State Finance Law caps gross debt at 60% of GDP. Watch debt-service-to-revenue ratio (~20%) for nearer-term fiscal stress.

aIDCDBTIIA.meaning: Public Debt, standardized — OECD-comparable framing of the gross public debt level in USD-equivalent terms.
aIDCDBTIIA.how_to_use: Use for international comparisons. Dollar-denominated framing exposes IDR depreciation effects on foreign-currency portion. Domestic analysts use IDR-level (aIDPDEBTA) for trend analysis.

aIDINVCHR/C.meaning: Increase in Stocks (Constant Prices) — inventory accumulation in real terms. Volatile GDP component.
aIDINVCHR/C.how_to_use: Inventory cycles drive ~0.5-1pp swings in quarterly GDP. Inventory build-ups during slowdowns (unintended) flag upcoming production cuts.

aIDGFCFR/C.meaning: Investment Spending (Constant Prices) — gross fixed capital formation in real terms. Same concept as aIDCGFCD/CA.
aIDGFCFR/C.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use either for investment-volume tracking.

aIDEXNGSR/C.meaning: Exports of Goods and Services (Constant) — real exports level for GDP-arithmetic. Companion to aIDCEXND/CA.
aIDEXNGSR/C.how_to_use: Use for export-volume tracking. Real exports growth is the meaningful trade-cycle signal.

aIDEXP.meaning: Exports — alternate framing of merchandise exports level. Cross-check against aIDCEXPB/A.
aIDEXP.how_to_use: Use either series for tracking; minor methodological/timing differences. The standardized version (aIDCEXPB/A) aligns with OECD frameworks.

aIDEXGAR.meaning: Exports Growth (Actual) — Reuters poll-anchored YoY export-growth release. Markets use as benchmark forecast anchor.
aIDEXGAR.how_to_use: Comparison against poll consensus drives IDR same-day. Indonesia export YoY swings 30+ pp through commodity cycles.

aIDEXPCRDA.meaning: Crude Petroleum Exports — Indonesia's crude oil exports. Indonesia is a net oil importer overall but exports some crude grades (mainly to Asian refiners).
aIDEXPCRDA.how_to_use: Small share of total exports (~1-2%). Has been declining structurally as domestic demand outpaces production. Indonesia left OPEC in 2008 and again in 2016 to align with importer status. Track Brent/WTI for unit-price impact.

aIDEXPGASA.meaning: Gas Exports — LNG plus pipeline gas exports. Indonesia is a major LNG exporter (Bontang, Tangguh terminals); main customers Japan, South Korea, China.
aIDEXPGASA.how_to_use: Highly correlated with Asian LNG spot prices (JKM benchmark). Long-term contracts dominate volume; spot prices drive quarterly revenue swings. Tangguh expansion (Train 3) boosted capacity in 2023.

aIDEXPNONG.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil and Gas — total non-O&G goods exports. ~90% of Indonesia's total goods exports.
aIDEXPNONG.how_to_use: Strip-out oil/gas removes commodity-price-driven swings, isolating manufactures + agri + minerals (coal, palm oil, nickel). Better cyclical signal than total exports.

aIDEXPNOGCH.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, China
aIDEXPNOGCH.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, China — exports to China. Indonesia's largest single export market (~25% of non-O&G exports).
aIDEXPNOGCH.how_to_use: Watch Chinese steel and EV production for leading signal. Coal + nickel + palm oil dominate. Falls sharply during China property-sector downturns (2022-23).

aIDEXPNDE.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, Germany
aIDEXPNDE.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, Germany — exports to Germany. ~2% of non-O&G exports. Largest items: palm oil derivatives, footwear, textiles, machinery.
aIDEXPNDE.how_to_use: Track for European demand cycle. EU palm-oil import restrictions (deforestation regulations) affect this flow.

aIDEXPJP.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, Japan
aIDEXPJP.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, Japan — exports to Japan. ~7-8% of non-O&G exports. Largest items: coal, copper concentrates, palm oil.
aIDEXPJP.how_to_use: Stable bilateral. Track JKM LNG prices for related gas-export effects (Japan is Indonesia's largest LNG buyer).

aIDEXPNMY.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, Malaysia
aIDEXPNMY.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, Malaysia — exports to Malaysia. ~5% of non-O&G exports. Heavy in CPO crude palm oil and intermediates.
aIDEXPNMY.how_to_use: Indonesia + Malaysia are world's two largest palm oil producers. Bilateral trade reflects cross-border processing chains.

aIDEXPSG.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, Singapore
aIDEXPSG.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, Singapore — exports to Singapore. ~7% of non-O&G exports. Significant trans-shipment hub effect.
aIDEXPSG.how_to_use: Singapore is largely a trans-shipment hub — a lot of Indonesia exports to Singapore are re-exported. Track for ASEAN trade flows.

aIDEXPUS.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, United States of America
aIDEXPUS.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, USA — exports to United States. ~10-12% of Indonesia's non-O&G exports.
aIDEXPUS.how_to_use: Heavy in textiles, apparel, footwear, electronics, palm oil. Track US-China trade tensions for trade-diversion benefits to Indonesia.

aIDEXPONG.meaning: Exports, Oil and Gas — Indonesia's oil + LNG exports. ~10% of total exports despite Indonesia being a net oil importer (gas exports offset oil imports).
aIDEXPONG.how_to_use: Tracks Brent/JKM (Asian LNG) prices closely. Pertamina dominates oil exports; multiple operators in LNG (Bontang, Tangguh).

aIDEXPETLA.meaning: Petroleum Product Exports — refined petroleum products (gasoline, diesel, fuel oil). Smaller than crude exports.
aIDEXPETLA.how_to_use: Niche. Pertamina (state oil company) exports surplus refined products from its refineries. Tracks regional refining margins.

aIDFDIYAR.meaning: FDI YoY change — pace of FDI inflow growth. Reuters-poll-anchored release.
aIDFDIYAR.how_to_use: Tracks BKPM realization data. Slowdowns flag investor-confidence loss.

aIDIMNGSR/C.meaning: Imports of Goods and Services (Constant) — real imports level for GDP accounting.
aIDIMNGSR/C.how_to_use: Use for import-volume tracking. Pairs with real exports (aIDEXNGSR/C) for net-export contribution to GDP.

aIDIMP.meaning: Imports — total merchandise imports level. Companion to aIDCIMPB/A.
aIDIMP.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data. Trade aggregates may differ slightly between BPS and BoP releases due to timing.

aIDIMGAR.meaning: Imports Growth (Actual) — Reuters poll-anchored YoY import-growth release.
aIDIMGAR.how_to_use: Surprise vs consensus drives IDR. Sustained import-growth above export-growth signals widening trade deficit.

aIDIMPCAP.meaning: Imports of Capital Goods — machinery, equipment, transport equipment. ~25% of total imports.
aIDIMPCAP.how_to_use: Leads investment (GFCF) by 1-2 quarters. Sustained surge signals upcoming capex acceleration. Falls during BI hike cycles.

aIDIMPCGS.meaning: Imports of Consumer Goods — finished consumer goods. Smallest share (~5%) reflecting domestic-manufacturing substitution policies.
aIDIMPCGS.how_to_use: Tracks middle-class import-luxury demand. Sensitive to IDR (expensive imports curtailed when IDR weakens).

aIDIMPNONG.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil and Gas — total non-O&G imports. ~85% of total imports.
aIDIMPNONG.how_to_use: Strip out oil/gas for a cleaner manufacturing-input demand signal. Tracks domestic manufacturing PMI.

aIDIMPCN.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, China
aIDIMPCN.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, China — imports from China. Indonesia's largest single import source (~30% of non-O&G imports).
aIDIMPCN.how_to_use: Heavy in machinery, electronics, base metals, chemicals. Tracks China's manufacturing capacity utilization. Indonesia runs persistent bilateral deficit with China.

aIDIMPNOGDE.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, Germany
aIDIMPNOGDE.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, Germany — imports from Germany. ~3% of non-O&G imports. Heavy in machinery, automotive equipment, chemicals.
aIDIMPNOGDE.how_to_use: Track for German auto-export and machinery cycle. EU-Indonesia trade tensions (palm oil restrictions, deforestation regulation) affect bilateral dynamics.

aIDIMPJP.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, Japan
aIDIMPJP.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, Japan — imports from Japan. ~10% of non-O&G imports. Heavy in machinery, transport equipment, electronics.
aIDIMPJP.how_to_use: Tracks Japanese auto + industrial-machinery exports. Stable bilateral.

aIDIMPNOGMY.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, Malaysia
aIDIMPNOGMY.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, Malaysia — imports from Malaysia. ~5% of non-O&G imports. ASEAN trade flows; petrochemicals, intermediates.
aIDIMPNOGMY.how_to_use: Track ASEAN regional supply-chain dynamics. Tariff harmonization under AEC supports this flow.

aIDIMPUS.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, USA
aIDIMPUS.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, USA — imports from USA. ~5% of non-O&G imports. Heavy in capital goods, agricultural products (soybeans, cotton).
aIDIMPUS.how_to_use: Track for US-Indonesia trade flows. Trump-era trade tensions (2018-2020, again 2025+) affect tariff-sensitive items.

aIDIMPONG.meaning: Imports, Oil and Gas — Indonesia's oil products + LPG imports. ~15% of total imports. Indonesia is a net oil importer (refining capacity short of consumption).
aIDIMPONG.how_to_use: Tracks Brent prices + IDR (cost-pass-through). Surges drive trade deficit and energy-subsidy bill. Major government-finance variable.

aIDIMPRM.meaning: Imports of Raw Materials — chemicals, base metals, industrial intermediates. ~70% of total imports — Indonesia's largest single import category.
aIDIMPRM.how_to_use: Tracks manufacturing-cycle inputs. Surges with manufacturing PMI. Used by analysts as a high-frequency manufacturing-output proxy.

aIDTRDAA.description: Indonesia, TRADE BALANCE (BLN OF $) (INITIAL), Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDTRDAA.meaning: Trade Balance (Initial release) — Reuters poll-anchored 'actual' trade balance. Used in surprise-vs-consensus tracking.
aIDTRDAA.how_to_use: Comparison against poll consensus drives IDR same-day at BPS release.

aIDTBAL.meaning: Trade Balance — total goods trade balance, alternative release. Same as aIDCVISB/A.
aIDTBAL.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

aIDCEXPPB/A.description: Merchandise Exports, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCEXPPB/A.meaning: Merchandise Exports, month-over-month change — high-frequency pulse on export momentum.
aIDCEXPPB/A.how_to_use: Highly volatile (±5-10% MoM is normal). Smooth with 3-month average. MoM useful for spotting turning points before YoY confirms.

aIDCEXPYB/A.description: Merchandise Exports, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCEXPYB/A.meaning: Merchandise Exports, year-over-year change — pace of export growth. Cleanest signal for trend.
aIDCEXPYB/A.how_to_use: Above 15% YoY = commodity-cycle peak; below -10% = downturn. Indonesia's export YoY swings 30+ pp through commodity cycles. Compare to non-commodity export growth (BPS publishes the breakdown) for underlying-demand vs price-driven growth.

aIDCEXPB/A.meaning: Merchandise Exports — total monthly goods exports published by BPS-Statistics Indonesia. Released ~3 weeks after month-end, alongside imports and trade balance.
aIDCEXPB/A.how_to_use: Most-watched Indonesia trade print. ~$22-25B/month recently. Decompose: oil/gas (~10%) vs non-oil/gas (~90%). Within non-oil/gas: coal, palm oil, nickel, manufactures. Surprise vs consensus (~$1B move) drives IDR. Use 3-month moving average for trend.

aIDCIMPPB/A.description: Merchandise Imports, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCIMPPB/A.meaning: Merchandise Imports, month-over-month change — high-frequency import-demand pulse.
aIDCIMPPB/A.how_to_use: Volatile. Smooth with 3-month MA for trend. Spike during Lebaran-Eid period (Q2 typically) for consumption-related imports.

aIDCIMPYB/A.description: Merchandise Imports, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCIMPYB/A.meaning: Merchandise Imports, year-over-year change — pace of import growth.
aIDCIMPYB/A.how_to_use: Pro-cyclical: surges with domestic demand and capital investment. Falls during IDR weakness episodes (cost-pass-through dampens demand). When import growth exceeds export growth for >2 quarters, current account deficit widens — IDR bearish.

aIDCIMPB/A.meaning: Merchandise Imports — total monthly goods imports from BPS. Largest categories: capital goods (~25%, machinery + transport eq), raw materials (~70%, chemicals + base metals + intermediates), consumer goods (~5%).
aIDCIMPB/A.how_to_use: Capital-goods imports lead investment by 2-3 quarters. Sustained surge in capital goods = upcoming GFCF acceleration. Raw materials track manufacturing PMI. Watch oil/gas imports — Indonesia is a net oil importer despite being a gas exporter.

aIDCVISB/A.meaning: Visible Trade Balance — monthly goods trade balance from BPS. Same conceptual measure as aIDCBOPA (BoP basis) at higher frequency. Computed as exports minus imports.
aIDCVISB/A.how_to_use: Indonesia has run a goods-trade surplus consistently since 2020 (~$30-40B annually) on commodity exports. Monthly surplus of $2-3B is normal; >$5B signals commodity-cycle peak. Surprises drive IDR same-day.

aIDCVISPB/A.description: Visible Trade Balance, month on month, Standardized, Absolute change
aIDCVISPB/A.meaning: Visible Trade Balance, MoM absolute change — month-over-month change in goods trade balance.
aIDCVISPB/A.how_to_use: Useful for tracking trade-balance momentum. Sharp swings (>$2B) reflect commodity-price shifts.

aIDCVISYB/A.description: Visible Trade Balance, year on year, Standardized, Absolute change
aIDCVISYB/A.meaning: Visible Trade Balance, year-over-year change — change in trade-balance level vs same month a year ago.
aIDCVISYB/A.how_to_use: Useful for tracking the pace of trade-balance expansion or compression. Sharp YoY decline (e.g., -$3B) signals deteriorating external surplus — IDR bearish.

aIDGNP.meaning: Gross National Product (GNP) — GDP plus net foreign factor income (factor receipts from abroad minus factor payments to abroad). Indonesia's GNP runs slightly below GDP because of net outflow of factor income (FDI dividends, debt-service payments).
aIDGNP.how_to_use: GNP-to-GDP gap measures the 'foreign income drain'. Indonesia's gap (-$25B/year) reflects FDI dividend repatriation and external debt service. The gap widens during commodity booms (more FDI profits to repatriate).

aIDPDBMT/C.meaning: Production: Basic Metals — output from Indonesia's metals processing industry. Includes nickel processing (smelters), copper (Freeport), aluminum (Inalum).
aIDPDBMT/C.how_to_use: Surged post-2020 with Indonesia's nickel-export ban driving downstream smelter buildout (Morowali, Weda Bay). Tracks global stainless steel and EV battery demand. Major growth narrative for the next decade.

aIDPDCHEMP/C.meaning: Production: Chemicals and Chemical Products — chemicals-sector output. Includes petrochemicals, fertilizers, industrial chemicals.
aIDPDCHEMP/C.how_to_use: Cyclical with global oil prices (petrochemical feedstocks) and agricultural cycles (fertilizers). Pertamina, Pupuk Indonesia (state fertilizer holding) are major operators.

aIDPDEMEQ.how_to_use: Tracks electrification investment and grid expansion. PLN's transmission/distribution buildout drives demand for transformers, switchgear, cables.

aIDPDMNEQ/C.meaning: Production: Machinery and Equipment NEC — capital-goods manufacturing. Tracks Indonesia's industrial-deepening cycle.
aIDPDMNEQ/C.how_to_use: Indonesia's machinery production share is small — most capital goods are imported. Surges signal local-content policy success.

aIDIPFOODH/C.meaning: Production: Manufacture of Food Products — food-and-beverage manufacturing output. Indonesia's largest single manufacturing sub-sector.
aIDIPFOODH/C.how_to_use: Stable, consumer-staple-driven. Tracks population growth and middle-class expansion. Major listed players: Indofood, Mayora, Wilmar.

aIDIPMANIDX.meaning: Manufacturing Production Index — BPS monthly manufacturing-only output. Subset of broader industrial production.
aIDIPMANIDX.how_to_use: Use for manufacturing-cycle tracking. Compare to S&P Global PMI manufacturing for cross-validation — when both move in same direction, signal is robust.

aIDIPMANQ.meaning: Manufacturing Production, Quarterly — BPS quarterly manufacturing output. Aggregates monthly data.
aIDIPMANQ.how_to_use: Use quarterly for GDP-component analysis (manufacturing GVA derives from this). Compare to manufacturing GVA (aIDVADGM/C) for cross-validation.

aIDPDMVTR/C.meaning: Production: Motor Vehicles, Trailers, Semitrailers — Indonesia's auto manufacturing output. Indonesia hosts ~1.4M unit/year auto production capacity.
aIDPDMVTR/C.how_to_use: Toyota, Daihatsu, Honda, Mitsubishi dominate (Japanese OEMs control ~95% of market). Auto exports to ASEAN, Middle East. Track for auto-sector cycle and ASEAN trade dynamics.

aIDPDRPP/C.meaning: Production: Rubber and Plastics Products — rubber + plastics-products manufacturing. Indonesia is a major natural rubber producer.
aIDPDRPP/C.how_to_use: Tracks consumer-goods (packaging, household plastics) and industrial (auto rubber components, hoses) demand. Watch alongside auto-industry cycle.

aIDPDTEXTP/C.meaning: Production: Textiles — textile-manufacturing output. Historically a major Indonesia export sector; now competing with Vietnam, Bangladesh.
aIDPDTEXTP/C.how_to_use: Sensitive to global apparel demand and IDR competitiveness. Indonesia textile sector has lost share to lower-wage Asia — sustained declines reflect this structural shift.

aIDPDWODXFR/C.description: Production, Wood & wood products except furniture
aIDPDWODXFR/C.meaning: Production: Wood and Wood Products (excl. Furniture) — wood-products manufacturing. Indonesia is a major plywood exporter; pulp & paper output also significant.
aIDPDWODXFR/C.how_to_use: Tracks global construction (plywood demand) and pulp-paper cycles. Concerns about deforestation and sustainable forestry (palm oil also implicated) drive ESG-policy attention.

aIDCINDYG/CA.description: Industrial Production Index, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCINDYG/CA.meaning: Industrial Production Index, year-over-year change — pace of manufacturing output growth.
aIDCINDYG/CA.how_to_use: Track trend; recent post-COVID recovery has shown 4-6% YoY. Sharp drops below zero signal manufacturing recession. Decompose by sector (food, chemicals, textiles, transport equipment) for source-of-weakness analysis.

aIDCINDG/A.meaning: Industrial Production Index, standardized — manufacturing output index. Published monthly by BPS with ~6-week lag.
aIDCINDG/A.how_to_use: Indonesia's industrial production tracking is less developed than DM peers — markets watch S&P Global Manufacturing PMI more closely. Use IPI for retrospective sector-mix analysis. Volatile due to small manufacturer sample.

aIDCINDPG/A.description: Industrial Production Index, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCINDPG/A.meaning: Industrial Production Index, MoM change — month-over-month industrial-output momentum.
aIDCINDPG/A.how_to_use: Volatile. Smooth with 3-month average for trend. Use YoY (aIDCINDYG/CA) for cyclical signal.

aIDONINTR.meaning: JIBOR Overnight (Jakarta Interbank Offered Rate) — the unsecured interbank borrowing rate at overnight tenor. Submitted daily by 18 contributor banks; published by BI at 10:00 WIB.
aIDONINTR.how_to_use: Most-watched short-term money market gauge. Trades within the BI corridor (DF rate floor, LF rate ceiling). Spikes during quarter-end and Lebanon (Eid) liquidity squeezes — BI typically smooths via repo operations. Monthly average tracks the policy rate closely; persistent deviation signals corridor stress.

aIDRREP7.description: Policy Rates, 7-day Reverse Repo Rate, Daily, Bank Indonesia
aIDRREP7.meaning: BI 7-Day Reverse Repo Rate, daily — the operational policy rate used to implement BI's monetary policy stance. Same level as the Main Policy Rate; this series captures the Reuters-sourced daily snapshot.
aIDRREP7.how_to_use: Daily-frequency series useful for tracking the date a rate change takes effect. RDG decisions are typically announced at 14:00 WIB and the new rate becomes effective the same day. Markets hedge ahead of meetings via 1M and 3M JIBOR — if JIBOR moves more than this rate, expect a near-term cut/hike.

aIDRREP7DR.description: Policy Rates, 7-day Reverse Repo Rate, Monthly, Bank Indonesia
aIDRREP7DR.meaning: BI 7-Day Reverse Repo Rate, monthly average — smoothed monthly version of the policy rate, useful for monthly-data comparisons (against CPI YoY, GDP, etc.).
aIDRREP7DR.how_to_use: Use the daily series (aIDRREP7) for high-frequency tracking; this monthly-averaged version pairs cleanly with monthly macro releases (M2, IDR fixings, FX reserves). The end-of-month value matches BI's headline policy stance.

aIDRINTO.description: Policy Rates, Bank Indonesia Deposits Facility
aIDRINTO.meaning: Bank Indonesia Deposits Facility (DF) Rate — the floor of BI's interest rate corridor. Banks place excess reserves with BI overnight at this rate. Set 100 bps below the BI 7-Day Reverse Repo Rate (the policy rate).
aIDRINTO.how_to_use: Defines the lower bound for short-term rates. JIBOR overnight (aIDONINTR) trades within the DF-LF corridor. When system liquidity is abundant, JIBOR drifts toward the DF rate; when tight, toward the LF rate. Spread vs policy rate (typically -100 bps) signals BI's corridor structure.

aIDRREPO.description: Policy Rates, Bank Indonesia Lending Facility
aIDRREPO.meaning: Bank Indonesia Lending Facility (LF) Rate — the ceiling of BI's interest rate corridor. Banks borrow overnight from BI at this rate when short of reserves. Set 100 bps above the BI 7-Day Reverse Repo Rate.
aIDRREPO.how_to_use: Defines the upper bound for short-term rates. Active in liquidity-stress episodes (e.g., 2020 COVID, 2022 EM stress) when JIBOR pushes toward the LF rate. Sustained borrowing at LF signals system-wide liquidity shortfall — BI typically responds with reserve requirement cuts or term repo operations.

aIDBIR.description: Policy Rates, Bank of Indonesia Main Policy Rate, now 7-day Reverse Repo Rate, Daily, Bank Indonesia
aIDBIR.meaning: Bank Indonesia (BI) Main Policy Rate — currently the BI 7-Day Reverse Repo Rate (BI7DRRR), which replaced the BI Rate as the official policy rate in August 2016. This is THE benchmark interest rate set by the Board of Governors at the monthly Bank Indonesia Monetary Policy Committee (RDG) meeting (third Wednesday of each month).
aIDBIR.how_to_use: The single most-watched Indonesia rate. Compare against the inflation target band (1.5-3.5% since 2024). BI's mandate combines inflation targeting with rupiah stability and growth — hike cycles often start to defend the IDR rather than fight inflation. Surprise vs consensus drives IDR, JCI, and SBN bond yields immediately. Track real rate (BI rate minus CPI YoY) — Indonesia traditionally runs positive real rates of 100-300 bps.

aIDPRATE.description: Policy Rates, Bank of Indonesia Main Policy Rate, now 7-day Reverse Repo Rate, Monthly, Bank Indonesia
aIDPRATE.meaning: Bank Indonesia Main Policy Rate — alternative release of the BI 7-Day Reverse Repo Rate at daily/snapshot frequency. Same conceptual rate as aIDBIR.
aIDPRATE.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDBIR for the latest setting. BI has held this rate in a 3.50-6.50% band over the post-2016 cycle; recent peak was 6.25% (April 2024 hike to defend IDR amid US dollar strength). Monthly RDG meeting decisions move IDR and SBN yields more than any other domestic data event.

aIDCBIRAR.meaning: Foreign Exchange Reserves (BMO release) — same conceptual measure as aIDCRESA in alternative classification. Cross-listed in interest-rates dataset.
aIDCBIRAR.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCRESA. The reserves level is critical for understanding BI's IDR-defense capacity.

aIDCONSAFI.meaning: Approved Foreign Investment — investment commitments approved by BKPM (Investment Coordinating Board). Quarterly release.
aIDCONSAFI.how_to_use: Approval ≠ realization. BKPM also publishes 'realization' data — typically realization runs 70-90% of approvals over 1-2 year window. Surge in approvals leads BoP FDI flows by 2-4 quarters.

aIDCONFRGAF.meaning: FDI inflows from Africa — minor FDI source. Mostly South Africa-routed mining-sector investments.
aIDCONFRGAF.how_to_use: Niche bilateral. Track for niche commodity-sector flows. Most African investment flows to Indonesia run through South African mining majors with Indonesian operations.

aIDCONFRGJP.meaning: FDI inflows from Japan — long-standing major FDI source. Japanese OEMs (Toyota, Honda, Mitsubishi) and trading houses (Mitsui, Marubeni, Sumitomo) dominate.
aIDCONFRGJP.how_to_use: ~10-15% of Indonesia FDI. Concentrated in autos, manufacturing, mining. Stable bilateral relationship. Monitor for major project announcements (e.g., new auto plants, gas field developments).

aIDCONFRGSG.meaning: FDI inflows from Singapore — largest single FDI source. Often pass-through capital from ultimate owners in HK, China, US, and other jurisdictions routing through Singapore for tax/legal reasons.
aIDCONFRGSG.how_to_use: Singapore consistently #1 FDI source (~30-40% of total). Flow swings driven by major M&A deals + new investment commitments. Track for total FDI cycle direction; less reliable for ultimate-owner attribution.

aIDCONFRGUS.meaning: FDI inflows from USA — US corporate investment in Indonesia. Smaller than Singapore/Japan FDI flows.
aIDCONFRGUS.how_to_use: Concentrated in oil/gas (ExxonMobil, Chevron historically), mining (Freeport), digital (data centers, internet platforms). Recent surge in semiconductor/AI infrastructure investment. Track for geopolitical-tilt signal — Indonesia values balance between US/China FDI sources.

aIDCONFRGUK.meaning: FDI inflows from United Kingdom — UK corporate investment in Indonesia. Concentrated in oil/gas (BP), banking (HSBC, Standard Chartered), retail.
aIDCONFRGUK.how_to_use: Tracks UK-Indonesia bilateral. Brexit effects re-routing some flows. Watch for trade-deal negotiations.

aIDCRCUPAA.description: Foreign currency reserves, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCRCUPAA.meaning: Foreign Currency Reserves, MoM change — month-over-month change in FX reserves.
aIDCRCUPAA.how_to_use: Sharp negative MoM (>3% drawdown) signals heavy FX intervention. Pair with IDR/USD performance for intervention-intensity signal.

aIDCRCUYWA.description: Foreign currency reserves, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCRCUYWA.meaning: Foreign Currency Reserves, YoY change — annual pace of FX reserves accumulation/depletion.
aIDCRCUYWA.how_to_use: Tracks structural reserve position. Surges during commodity-export booms (BI accumulates); depletion during EM-stress episodes.

aIDCRCUCPA.meaning: Foreign Currency Reserves (Standardized) — companion to aIDFXRES at standardized framing. The FX-only component of total reserves.
aIDCRCUCPA.how_to_use: Use for cross-country comparisons. Indonesia FX reserves cover ~6 months of imports — comfortable per IMF adequacy metrics.

aIDCRESPA.description: Official international reserves, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCRESPA.meaning: Official International Reserves, MoM change — month-over-month change in total reserves (FX + gold + IMF position + SDRs).
aIDCRESPA.how_to_use: Highest-frequency reserves trend signal. Most-watched data point each first Friday when BI releases.

aIDCRESYA.description: Official international reserves, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCRESYA.meaning: Official International Reserves, YoY change — annual pace of total reserves accumulation.
aIDCRESYA.how_to_use: Smooths out monthly volatility. Indonesia reserves typically grow 3-7% pa during normal cycles; depletion in EM-stress years (-5 to -15%).

aIDCRESA.meaning: Official International Reserves — total foreign exchange reserves held by Bank Indonesia. Includes FX assets, gold, IMF position, and SDRs. Published monthly (typically first Friday) by BI.
aIDCRESA.how_to_use: Critical for IDR defense. Recent levels ~$140-150B, providing ~6 months of import cover (vs IMF safe minimum of 3 months). Sharp drawdowns (>$5B in a month) signal heavy FX intervention to defend IDR — historically marks IDR weakness peaks. Build-ups during commodity surpluses absorbed via BI's FX purchases.

aIDFXRAA.meaning: Reserves — alternative release of total international reserves. Same as aIDCRESA at different vintage.
aIDFXRAA.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences are typically minor.

aIDFXRES.meaning: Foreign currency reserves — the FX-only component of total international reserves (excludes gold, IMF position, SDRs). The most actively-managed portion of BI reserves.
aIDFXRES.how_to_use: ~95% of total reserves. Composition: ~60% USD, ~20% EUR, ~10% JPY/CNY (BI does not publish exact split). Drawn down for FX intervention; replenished via commodity-export FX accumulation. Pair with monthly IDR/USD performance for intervention intensity signal.

aIDREIN.meaning: Reserves, International — alternative release of total international reserves.
aIDREIN.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

aIDRVSFX.description: Reserves, Reserve in foreign exchange, currency and deposits
aIDRVSFX.meaning: Reserves: Foreign Exchange, Currency and Deposits — the FX cash + bank deposits component of reserves. Most-liquid portion, used for daily FX operations and short-term IDR defense.
aIDRVSFX.how_to_use: Subset of aIDFXRES (which also includes securities held in custody). The currency/deposits portion is the immediately-deployable defense buffer. Tracks BI's day-to-day FX intervention capacity.

aIDRESOA.meaning: Reserves: Reserve Others — non-FX, non-gold, non-IMF residual reserve assets. Small.
aIDRESOA.how_to_use: Niche. Captures other-claims items not classified into FX/gold/SDR/IMF position.

aIDRESVFUND.description: Reserves, Reserve position in the fund
aIDRESVFUND.meaning: Reserves: Reserve Position in the Fund — Indonesia's reserve tranche position at the IMF. Funds Indonesia can withdraw on demand without conditions.
aIDRESVFUND.how_to_use: Niche. Used in BoP accounting; rarely activated. Small relative to FX reserves (~$1B vs ~$140B FX).

aIDRES.meaning: Reserves: Reserve Total — same conceptual measure as aIDCRESA (total international reserves) at potentially different release vintage.
aIDRES.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data. The standardized aIDCRESA aligns with IMF SDDS reporting standards.

aIDRESGLD.meaning: Gold reserves component of international reserves. Bank Indonesia holds ~78 metric tons of gold (small relative to reserve-currency central banks).
aIDRESGLD.how_to_use: Slow-moving. Stock unchanged for years; valuation moves with gold price (USD per troy ounce). Larger central banks (China, India, Russia) have been net gold buyers post-2020; BI has been broadly neutral. Useful for tracking total-reserve composition trends but not actively managed.

aIDRESSDR.meaning: Reserves: SDR Holdings — Special Drawing Rights at the IMF. Reserve asset created by IMF; valued by basket of major currencies (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP).
aIDRESSDR.how_to_use: Boosted in August 2021 IMF general SDR allocation ($650B globally; Indonesia received ~$6.3B). Stable since. Useful for tracking IMF reserve operations but not actively managed.

aIDGCINV.meaning: Gross Capital Formation, Capital Investment Index — total investment level (GFCF + inventories).
aIDGCINV.how_to_use: Use GFCF (aIDCGFCD/CA) for the cleaner investment-cycle signal. GCF includes inventories which add volatility.

aIDGFIT/C.description: GFCF, Current Prices, Investment / Capital Formation, Quarterly, Statistics Indonesia
aIDGFIT/C.meaning: GFCF (Current Prices) — gross fixed capital formation in nominal terms.
aIDGFIT/C.how_to_use: Use constant-prices version (aIDGFCFR/C) for real cycle. Nominal version useful in fiscal arithmetic.

aIDM1.meaning: Money Supply M1 (method break Jan 2011) — narrow money level. Methodology revised in 2011 to align with international standards.
aIDM1.how_to_use: Pre/post-2011 series not directly comparable due to methodology break. Use post-2011 data for trend analysis. M1 = currency in circulation + demand deposits at banks.

aIDM2.meaning: Money Supply M2 — broad money level published by Bank Indonesia. Includes M1 (currency + demand deposits) plus quasi-money (time deposits, savings deposits, foreign currency deposits at banks).
aIDM2.how_to_use: Track YoY growth (aIDM2AR) for cyclical signal. Foreign currency deposit share — when it rises sharply, indicates IDR mistrust (dollarization). Recent share ~15-18% of M2; spikes during IDR weakness episodes.

aIDM2AR.meaning: Money Supply M2, YoY change — alternative release of broad money growth rate.
aIDM2AR.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCMS2YB/A. The headline M2 growth gauge for monetary-policy analysis.

aIDMSC.meaning: Money Supply Currency — currency in circulation outside the banking system. Subset of M1.
aIDMSC.how_to_use: Tracks public's cash demand. Indonesia is still cash-heavy (digital payment adoption growing rapidly post-2020). Lebaran-Eid drives the largest annual cash spike.

aIDCMS0B/A.meaning: Money Supply M0 (Monetary Base) — currency in circulation plus banks' reserve deposits at Bank Indonesia. Direct BI liability that expands with reserve creation.
aIDCMS0B/A.how_to_use: Distinct from M1/M2 — captures BI balance-sheet expansion. Useful for tracking unconventional easing periods (2020-22 BI bond purchases). Compare to M2 for the bank-lending multiplier (currently ~6x).

aIDCMS0PB/A.description: Money Supply M0, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCMS0PB/A.meaning: Money Supply M0, month-over-month change — high-frequency monetary-base pulse.
aIDCMS0PB/A.how_to_use: Volatile. Smooth with 3-month average for trend. Spikes around Lebaran-Eid as currency demand surges (cash withdrawals for holiday).

aIDCMS0YB/A.description: Money Supply M0, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCMS0YB/A.meaning: Money Supply M0, year-over-year change — pace of monetary base expansion.
aIDCMS0YB/A.how_to_use: M0 growth signals BI's stance. Surges 2020-22 reflected COVID-era unconventional easing (burden-sharing with Treasury). Track for unconventional policy signals.

aIDCMS1B/A.meaning: Money Supply M1 (Standardized) — narrow money level (currency + demand deposits). Most-liquid money aggregate.
aIDCMS1B/A.how_to_use: Use level for analytical baseline; YoY (aIDCMS1YB/A) for cyclical signal. M1 leads economic activity by 2-4 months.

aIDCMS1PB/A.description: Money Supply M1, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCMS1PB/A.meaning: Money Supply M1, MoM percent change — high-frequency narrow-money pulse.
aIDCMS1PB/A.how_to_use: Volatile (Lebaran cash demand drives big swings). Smooth with 3-month average. Use YoY for trend.

aIDCMS1YB/A.description: Money Supply M1, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCMS1YB/A.meaning: Money Supply M1, year-over-year change — narrow money (currency in circulation + demand deposits at banks). The most-liquid money aggregate.
aIDCMS1YB/A.how_to_use: M1 growth leads economic activity by 2-4 months because it captures transaction demand. M1 acceleration ahead of GDP suggests upcoming activity pickup. Pair with M2 — divergence (M1 up, M2 flat) signals shift from time deposits to demand (lower interest rates, weaker savings incentive).

aIDCMS2PB/A.description: Money Supply M2, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCMS2PB/A.meaning: Money Supply M2, month-over-month change — high-frequency broad-money pulse.
aIDCMS2PB/A.how_to_use: Volatile. Smooth with 3-month average. Sustained MoM contraction (rare) signals tight liquidity.

aIDCMS2YB/A.description: Money Supply M2, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCMS2YB/A.meaning: Money Supply M2, year-over-year change — broad money including currency, demand deposits, time/savings deposits, and money market mutual funds. The headline Indonesia liquidity gauge published monthly by Bank Indonesia.
aIDCMS2YB/A.how_to_use: Indonesia M2 typically grows 6-10% YoY in normal cycles. Sustained sub-5% signals tight liquidity (often during BI hike cycles); >12% suggests aggressive easing or external inflows (commodity boom). Pair with credit growth — when M2 rises faster than credit, banks are accumulating liquid assets (gov bonds) rather than lending.

aIDCMS2B/A.meaning: Money Supply M2 (Standardized) — broad money level. Companion to aIDM2 in standardized framing.
aIDCMS2B/A.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDM2. Use YoY (aIDCMS2YB/A) for the cyclical signal.

aIDFRGART.meaning: Foreign Tourist Arrivals — international visitor arrivals to Indonesia. Bali dominates (40-50% of arrivals); Jakarta and Batam also significant.
aIDFRGART.how_to_use: Pre-COVID peak ~16M/year (2019); collapsed to ~4M (2020-21); recovered to ~12M (2024). Tourism is ~5% of GDP. Watch for service-deficit narrowing as arrivals normalize.

aIDTOURARR.description: Foreign tourist arrivals through 3 airports & Batam island
aIDTOURARR.meaning: Foreign Tourist Arrivals through 3 Airports & Batam Island — high-frequency tourism gauge from major entry points (Soekarno-Hatta Jakarta, Ngurah Rai Bali, Kualanamu Medan, Batam).
aIDTOURARR.how_to_use: Higher-frequency than total arrivals (aIDFRGART). Monthly. Useful for spotting recovery momentum or shocks (volcano eruptions, terrorism, geopolitics).

aIDOAPPPGR.meaning: PPP for GDP — purchasing power parity conversion factor. Number of IDR with the same purchasing power as 1 USD in the US economy.
aIDOAPPPGR.how_to_use: Currently ~Rp 4,500 per USD (vs market exchange rate ~Rp 16,000/USD). Large gap reflects Indonesia's lower price level — a $1 in Indonesia buys ~3.5x what $1 buys in the US for typical goods.

aIDCNPERR/C.meaning: Private Consumer Spending, constant prices — household final consumption expenditure component of GDP. Same conceptual measure as aIDCPCED/CA in different framing.
aIDCNPERR/C.how_to_use: Use aIDCPCEYD/A for YoY pace; this level series for analytical baseline. Indonesia's private consumption share of GDP (~55%) is high vs East Asian peers (40-50%) — reflects services-economy structure.

aIDZGVCOP.description: IFDI, Governance, Corporate Governance, Average Share of Independent Directors on the Board
aIDZGVCOP.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator (IFDI): Governance, Corporate Governance, Average Share of Independent Directors on the Board. Reference data on Indonesia's Islamic finance ecosystem (Sharia-compliant banking, takaful insurance, sukuk markets, Islamic funds).
aIDZGVCOP.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.

aIDAWMAOTA.meaning: Average Monthly Wages — average net wage of formal-sector employees, published by BPS in the Sakernas (National Labor Force Survey).
aIDAWMAOTA.how_to_use: Indonesia minimum wages are set provincially (UMP) and revised annually. Average monthly wages run well above minimum (urban formal sector ~Rp 3-4 million; minimum wage range Rp 2-5 million by province). Watch annual UMP decisions in late-Q4 for next year's labor-cost trajectory.

aIDAWMAOTR.description: Average Monthly Wages, Average, Chg Y/Y
aIDAWMAOTR.meaning: Average Monthly Wages, year-over-year change — wage growth rate.
aIDAWMAOTR.how_to_use: Indonesia wage growth typically runs 5-8% YoY (well above CPI inflation 2-3%, real wage growth ~3-5%). Sharp acceleration signals minimum-wage hikes; deceleration signals labor-market slack.

aIDMNAVWGMF.meaning: Monthly Average Wage — Manufacturing — average wage in the manufacturing sector specifically.
aIDMNAVWGMF.how_to_use: Track manufacturing wages for unit-labor-cost trends. Indonesia competes with Vietnam, Bangladesh, India on labor-cost competitiveness in light manufacturing — sustained wage growth above productivity growth signals erosion.

aIDLFTOT.meaning: Total Labour Force — employed + unemployed. People aged 15+ either working or actively seeking work. From BPS Sakernas.
aIDLFTOT.how_to_use: Indonesia labor force ~143M (2024), growing ~1-1.5% annually with demographic expansion. Labor-force participation rate ~70% (men) and ~55% (women) — female participation gap is a major reform priority.

aIDUEMP.meaning: Unemployment — total unemployed persons. Same conceptual measure as aIDWKUNTTP.
aIDUEMP.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Indonesia open unemployment ~7.5M (2024). Pair with the rate (aIDUNR) for cycle interpretation.

aIDUNHTOTR.meaning: Open Unemployment Rate — official BPS unemployment rate. Same conceptual measure as aIDUNR with possible vintage difference.
aIDUNHTOTR.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever is fresher. Indonesia structural rate ~5%; cyclical bottom around 4.5%; recession peak ~7% (2020).

aIDUNR.meaning: Unemployment Rate — share of the labor force without jobs but actively seeking work. Published twice a year by BPS via the Sakernas (National Labor Force Survey), with February and August reference periods.
aIDUNR.how_to_use: Indonesia structural unemployment rate around 5-6%. Spiked to 7.1% in August 2020 (COVID) then declined. Underemployment (workers on <35hr/week) is much higher (~25%) — formal unemployment understates labor-market slack. Watch youth unemployment (15-24 yo) which runs 3x the headline rate (~17%).

aIDCEMFO/A.description: Employment, Labour Force Survey, Standardized (based on source annual data)
aIDCEMFO/A.meaning: Employment, Labour Force Survey (Standardized) — total employed from BPS Sakernas. Reference labor-market level for productivity calculations.
aIDCEMFO/A.how_to_use: Indonesia total employment ~135M (2024). Use alongside GDP to compute output-per-worker (productivity). Productivity growth ~2-3% pa — positive but below DM rates.

aIDCUNPPP.description: Unemployment Level, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aIDCUNPPP.meaning: Unemployment Level, month-over-month change — but Sakernas is biannual so MoM is interpolated.
aIDCUNPPP.how_to_use: Use the level (aIDCUNPP) and YoY (aIDCUNPYP) for primary analysis. MoM has limited signal value given the underlying biannual data.

aIDCUNPYP.description: Unemployment Level, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aIDCUNPYP.meaning: Unemployment Level, year-over-year change — pace of unemployment increase or decrease.
aIDCUNPYP.how_to_use: Track for cyclical labor-market dynamics. Sharp YoY rises (>10%) signal recession-like conditions. Indonesia rarely shows such moves outside crisis (1998, 2020).

aIDCUNPP.meaning: Unemployment Level (Standardized) — total unemployed persons in standardized framing.
aIDCUNPP.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDUEMP/aIDWKUNTTP. The standardized version aligns with ILO methodology.

aIDCUNPQ/A.description: Unemployment rate, Standardized (based on source annual data)
aIDCUNPQ/A.meaning: Unemployment Rate, standardized (annual) — OECD-comparable framing of the BPS unemployment rate. Used for cross-country comparisons.
aIDCUNPQ/A.how_to_use: Use the headline aIDUNR series for domestic analysis; this standardized version aligns with ILO methodology for international benchmarking. Indonesia's rate has been falling structurally from ~10% (2005) to ~5% (2024) as the labor market absorbs young workers.

aIDRSLSAR.meaning: Retail Sales, year-over-year change — Bank Indonesia's monthly Retail Sales Survey result. Released ~6 weeks after month-end.
aIDRSLSAR.how_to_use: Most-watched Indonesia retail-demand gauge. Recent YoY ~3-5%. Surges around Lebaran-Eid month. Decompose by category (food, clothing, automotive, fuel) for cyclical-mix signal. Pair with consumer confidence (aIDCONCF) for triangulated read.

aIDRSLSM.meaning: Retail Sales Total Index (rebased) — BI Retail Sales Survey level. Tracks aggregate sales across major retailers.
aIDRSLSM.how_to_use: Use the YoY series (aIDRSLSAR) for trend; level for analytical baseline. Indonesia retail surveys are broad (food + non-food combined) — narrower than US-style retail-control concepts.
